articles.title: Why Did The NFL Suspend Bears Defender Montez Sweat For 2 Games?
articles.summary: The NFL has reportedly suspended Chicago Bears defensive lineman Montez Sweat for two games.
articles.body: On Sunday, the Chicago Bears lost to their bitter rival, the Green Bay Packers, 31-7. And on Tuesday, they lost one of their best defenders to a suspension. The Bears announced on Tuesday afternoon that the NFL has suspended Chicago defensive lineman Montez Sweat, who will miss two games without pay due to a violation of the league's Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy, per NFL Media. Through five games, Sweat has totaled two sacks and seven combined tackles. Chicago's defense is tied for fifth in the NFL in opponent points (19.2 per game), is ninth outright in both opponent total yards (311.4 per game) and opponent rushing yards (96.0 per game), 12th in opponent passing yards (215.4 per game) and tied for 13th in sacks (11.0). Sweat will now miss Chicago's Week 6 road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons (Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX) and its Week 7 Thursday night home bout against the defending AFC-champion New England Patriots (Oct. 22). Last season (2025), Sweat racked up 10.0 sacks, three forced fumbles, five passes defended and 53 combined tackles. Sweat, who's in the third season of a four-year, $98 million deal, is in his third complete season with the Bears and fourth season altogether with the franchise; Chicago acquired Sweat, a 2019 first-round pick, from the Washington Commanders during the 2023 season for its 2024 second-round pick. Elsewhere, the 3-2 Bears have been without starting quarterback Caleb Williams since Week 2 due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum have each started in place of Williams, who's expected to return to action in the near future.

articles.title: Julian Sayin vs. Josh Hoover: Two Different Paths, Same Championship Ambitions
articles.summary: Julian Sayin and Josh Hoover took different paths to college football stardom. Now, they’ll face off in a showdown with major Big Ten and national title implications.
articles.body: What do a five-star quarterback from California who once committed to play for Nick Saban and a three-star prospect from Texas who nearly started his career at Indiana have in common? More than you might think. Ohio State's Julian Sayin and Indiana's Josh Hoover took different paths to get where they are today, but both share the same goal of winning a national championship. Two Paths To Stardom: Sayin vs. Hoover Julian Sayin was supposed to be the next big thing at Alabama. A five-star recruit, he committed to the Crimson Tide with plans to play for Saban. Then Saban retired, and Sayin’s plans changed. He pivoted to Ohio State — a decision that has worked out pretty well for both sides. Sayin spent the 2024 season learning from the sideline, serving as the backup to Kansas State transfer Will Howard. While Sayin waited, Howard led the Buckeyes on a College Football Playoff run that ended with a national championship. Then it was Sayin’s turn. Taking over the Ohio State offense came with a bonus that any quarterback would dream about: Jeremiah Smith. I had the luxury of throwing to Jeff Samardzija, Anthony Fasano and Maurice Stovall during my time at Notre Dame. I quickly learned that an elite pass-catcher can be a quarterback's best friend, and Sayin and Smith have developed a strong connection. Sayin is finding his star receiver again and again as Smith continues to rewrite the Buckeyes’ record book. Sayin is best described as a point guard within Ohio State's offense. He distributes the ball, gets it to his playmakers and rarely gives it away. Through his career, he has thrown 50 touchdowns to just 10 interceptions while completing passes at an elite rate. Last season, his 77% completion rate ranked third in FBS history. When I spoke with Sayin earlier this week, he pointed out one area he wanted to improve this season: using his legs to put more stress on opposing defenses. So far, that work has paid off, as he has already rushed for two touchdowns after failing to score on the ground last season. He has become more willing to scramble for a first down or extend a play when the pocket breaks down. Just look at what he did against Illinois. There's still one big question Sayin must answer in Saturday's game against Indiana: Can he handle the Hoosiers' pressure? If Sayin wants to follow in Howard's footsteps and lead Ohio State to another national championship, he'll need to show he can stay composed when defenses turn up the heat. In the Buckeyes' biggest games, pressure has been his biggest vulnerability. Sayin is an incredibly accurate passer, but his completion percentage drops by nearly 20 percentage points when he's under pressure. You better believe Indiana defensive coordinator Bryant Haines will test Sayin to see if he can beat the blitz. Hoover took a very different path from Sayin to get to where he is today. A three-star recruit out of the Dallas metroplex, Hoover was originally committed to Indiana before flipping to TCU to stay closer to home. After redshirting and spending a year backing up quarterback Chandler Morris, he took over as the Horned Frogs’ full-time starter in 2024. By the time he left Fort Worth, Hoover had nearly three years of starting experience, close to 10,000 passing yards and more than 70 touchdowns. This production and experience made Hoover a prime target for Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and his staff, who have gone to the transfer portal for a QB in five straight years dating back to their time at James Madison. Once again, they’ve found a veteran who fits their system — and Hoover looks right at home in offensive coordinator Mike Shanahan’s offense. Indiana’s attack gives Hoover plenty of opportunities to play to his strengths, from quick passes in the RPO game to back-shoulder throws when the Hoosiers push the ball downfield. He’s stepped in and made it look seamless. In fact, Hoover has the highest completion percentage among Big Ten quarterbacks on throws released in under 2.5 seconds. If there was one criticism during Hoover's time at TCU, it would be turnovers, and they became a topic of conversation in the offseason. So far, he’s answered emphatically, throwing 17 touchdowns without an interception, putting those concerns firmly in the rearview mirror. Now comes the chance for both quarterbacks to make a statement. For Hoover, it’s about justifying his decision to come to Indiana. A win over the Buckeyes would prove that this program isn't just some flash in the pan. Big players deliver in big moments. This is Hoover's chance to do just that. Sayin, meanwhile, has a chance to deliver the kind of signature performance that can put Ohio State back on top of the Big Ten. The Buckeyes haven’t won a Big Ten title since 2020, and beating Indiana would be a major step toward changing that. There may not be a better time for Sayin to make his mark. One Name To Know … Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State With the first pick of the 2027 NFL Draft … Yes, that's right, Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker is giving off those sorts of vibes. The Cowboys' gun-slinger is turning heads and has the No. 18 team in the country dreaming of a Big 12 title and a spot in the CFP. NFL scouts are jumping to take a trip to Stillwater to munch on some Eskimo Joes and watch the prodigy sling it. To appreciate the story of Mestemaker, one has to understand his journey. Mestemaker never started a game at quarterback in high school. In fact, he attempted just 30 passes in his entire prep career — as a backup. Labeled a zero-star recruit, he was offered a walk-on spot at North Texas under head coach Eric Morris. Even then, a path to playing time was far from guaranteed. Mestemaker arrived at fall camp fifth on the depth chart before working his way into the backup role. His first chance to start finally came at the end of the season, when starting quarterback Chandler Morris entered the transfer portal ahead of the First Responder Bowl against Texas State. Mestemaker made the most of the opportunity, throwing for nearly 400 yards and two touchdowns while adding another 70 yards and a score on the ground, and giving Morris a glimpse of what he could become. Two interceptions and a North Texas loss put a damper on the performance, but there was enough there to suggest the Mean Green might have found something special in the inexperienced quarterback. Heading into the 2025 season, Mestemaker won the starting job over Miami transfer Ross Poffenbarger. He rewrote the North Texas record books in his first season as a starter and earned American Conference Offensive Player of the Year honors. Fast-forward to 2026, and Mestemaker followed Morris to Stillwater, Oklahoma, with a mission to bring Oklahoma State’s offense back to life. So far, he’s delivering. The junior leads the Big 12 in passing touchdowns with 13 while guiding the Cowboys to a 4-1 start. Mestemaker’s unlikely path has drawn comparisons to Ryan Tannehill, who initially committed to Texas A&M as a quarterback before spending his first few seasons with the Aggies at wide receiver. Tannehill eventually returned to quarterback for the final season and a half of his college career, setting the stage for his eventual NFL success. What stands out most about Mestemaker is his feel for finding windows in coverage. Despite his limited experience, he plays like a seasoned veteran. He’ll occasionally take unnecessary risks and put the ball in harm’s way, but that generally comes as a result of the sheer volume of passes he's throwing. Mestemaker averages 34 pass attempts per game, the most in the Big 12, and the game situation sometimes calls for him to take chances. He’s also a threat with his legs, showing the toughness to fight his way into the end zone. This week, the Pokes hit the road to take on Houston in what could be their toughest Big 12 test yet. For Mestemaker, it’s a chance to make a statement against a quality opponent and take another step up the NFL Draft boards. What I'm Watching … BYU vs. Notre Dame Since this is my column, I might as well be honest about what I’ll actually be watching Saturday night: my Fighting Irish taking on a top-10 opponent on the road in their toughest test of the season to date. This matchup has no shortage of storylines, and it’s been months in the making. Remember when Notre Dame opted out of the Pop-Tarts Bowl after getting snubbed by the College Football Playoff? Well, that game would have been against BYU, which went on to win and bask in the glory of a giant Pop-Tart. Personally, I’m more of a brown sugar cinnamon guy. This game came together after the Notre Dame-USC rivalry fell through. BYU agreed to host the Irish during the open date typically occupied by USC in even-numbered years, setting up a trip to Provo as the leaves change across the heartland. Rather than heading west to Southern California, Notre Dame will make the trek into the mountains of Utah for what should be a picturesque setting and a terrific atmosphere. I remember opening our season at BYU in 2004. We had no idea what we were walking into. LaVell Edwards Stadium was rocking, and Cougar fans were hopped up on sugar and altitude. It was a nasty environment. We had beaten BYU rather handily the previous season in South Bend, 33-14. But this time, the Cougars threw a pressure package at us that took until the second half to figure out. By then, it was too late. There won’t be many surprises this time around. Both teams have enough film on each other to understand what the other wants to do, and both have experienced quarterbacks who have command of their respective offenses: Bear Bachmeier for BYU and CJ Carr for Notre Dame. Their styles, however, couldn’t be much different. Carr operates from the pocket like a prototypical NFL quarterback. He diagnoses defenses before the snap, identifies potential weaknesses and looks to exploit them through the air. Bachmeier can hurt defenses on designed quarterback runs, but he's also a very alert runner on passing downs. Give him an opening, and he’ll tuck the ball and take off. For Notre Dame, a win would validate the dominance it has shown so far this season. For BYU, it’s a chance to prove the Cougars belong among the nation’s elite. The experts in the desert have the Cougars as a double-digit home underdog. articles.title: Mariners Reportedly Targeting 4 Managers With Championship Pedigree
articles.summary: Here are some of the candidates the Seattle Mariners are reportedly considering for their next manager.
articles.body: Following the departure of Dan Wilson, the Seattle Mariners are doing their due diligence as they search outside the organization for their next manager. According to Jon Heyman of the New York Post, the Mariners are "casting a wide net" of candidates that includes a mixture of former managers. The organization is prioritizing managerial experience as a key component of what they’re looking for in their next skipper. In the wake of Wilson’s departure, ownership seems intent on finding stability in the dugout. To do so, the Mariners would have to break a long-running organizational trend. They haven't hired a manager with prior major league experience since Lloyd McClendon in 2013, a tenure that lasted just two seasons. Here are some of the candidates Seattle is reportedly considering: Joe EspadaAstros Manager As things stand, Espada could be a frontrunner for the job. The Mariners have already received permission to speak with Espada, whose contract is expiring following the Astros' Wild Card loss to the Chicago White Sox. If the Mariners can poach Espada from an in-division rival, it wouldn't be without precedent. The Chicago Cubs pulled off a similar maneuver when they lured Craig Counsell away from the Milwaukee Brewers in 2023. Espada brings strong experience, having won the 2022 World Series as the Astros' bench coach under Dusty Baker. Over the past three seasons as Houston's manager, he compiled a 256–229 record along with two AL West division titles. Rocco BaldelliFormer Twins Manager With former managers on the Mariners' radar, they are showing interest in ex-Minnesota Twins skipper Rocco Baldelli. After being let go by the Twins following the 2025 season, he spent this season with the Los Angeles Dodgers as an executive in baseball operations. Before transitioning into coaching, Baldelli spent seven seasons in the majors playing for the Tampa Bay Rays and Boston Red Sox. He then rejoined the Rays' front office and coaching staff from 2015 to 2018, serving as a special assistant, first base coach and field coordinator. After spending three seasons under manager Kevin Cash, Baldelli left to take over the Twins in 2019. He was named AL Manager of the Year as a rookie skipper and went on to spend seven seasons with the Twins, posting a 527–505 record while securing three AL Central division titles. Brandon HydeFormer Orioles Manager Sticking with AL experience as a managerial candidate, the Mariners could look toward former Baltimore Orioles manager Brandon Hyde. He brings substantial experience leading a rebuild into a contender, along with prior coaching stints with the Chicago Cubs and the then-Florida Marlins. Hyde made a name for himself by turning a rebuilding Orioles squad into a legitimate contender in a competitive AL East. Not only did he post three straight winning seasons, but that run was capped by a 101-win campaign in 2023, where he won AL Manager of the Year. He also played a big role in developing young core talent like Adley Rutschman, Gunnar Henderson and Jordan Westburg. After Baltimore let Hyde go 43 games into last season, he took on a senior advisor role with the in-division Rays. David RossFormer Cubs Manager After spending the past few seasons out of the dugout, former Cubs skipper David Ross is a name that could surface as a serious managerial candidate. He posted a respectable 15-year MLB career as a player and won World Series titles with the Red Sox in 2013 and the Cubs in 2016. Following his retirement, Ross stepped directly into managing when he replaced Joe Maddon ahead of the 2020 season. Ross’ tenure in Chicago came with mixed results during a period of roster transition, as he compiled a 262-284 record across four seasons with just one playoff appearance. He was dismissed from the Cubs in 2023, and they eventually replaced him with Counsell. If the Mariners want prior managerial experience alongside a two-time World Series champion who won rings in both leagues, Ross checks all of those boxes.

articles.title: Mahomes Mountain Week 6: Jared Goff Rises, Patrick Mahomes Remains At The Summit
articles.summary: Nick Wright’s quarterback hierarchy saw a handful of names tumble this week but one name stayed at the top of the mountain.
articles.body: Nick Wright’s quarterback hierarchy saw a handful of names tumble this week but one signal caller stayed at the top of the mountain: Patrick Mahomes is alone at the summit. Jalen Hurts falls again, Dak Prescott drops after an underwhelming Thursday night, and Matthew Stafford actually climbs despite a loss — while a trio of backups quietly moved up the board. Here’s how Wright sees the league’s quarterbacks this week: Injured: Lamar JacksonBaltimore Ravens Caleb WilliamsChicago Bears Baker MayfieldTampa Bay Buccaneers Jaxson DartNew York Giants Wright's thoughts: "Off the mountain, injured and off the mountain because of performance. Injured: Lamar should be back, Caleb should be back, Baker should be back. Jaxson Dart won’t be back." Off the mountain: Justin HerbertLos Angeles Chargers Tyson BagentChicago Bears Malik WillisMiami Dolphins Cam WardTennessee Titans Wright's thoughts: "Cam Ward, Malik Willis, Tyson Bagent — yikes. And Justin Herbert, who I don’t see, how, right now, he’s not one of the 28 best quarterbacks in the league. They got the ball back down six, and I felt like they had no shot whatsoever. I don’t know what’s wrong. We’ll talk about him later." 7th Row: Jalen HurtsPhiladelphia Eagles Daniel JonesIndianapolis Colts Deshaun WatsonCleveland Browns Bo NixDenver Broncos Geno SmithNew York Jets Jacoby BrissettArizona Cardinals Jameis WinstonNew York Giants Wright: "Bottom of the mountain. Jalen Hurts has to fall again. I understand there’s a lot working against him, the injuries, the retirement [of offensive tackle Lane Johnson], the head coach — I get it. But the offense is also not functional. His whole thing had been, hey, the stats might not be pretty, but we’re winning. You don’t have that either on a three-game losing streak. He tumbles a bit. "Daniel Jones, Deshaun Watson drop a bit. Bo Nix, Geno Smith and Jacoby Brissett, Jameis Winston — they’re probably bottom-row guys at this point in their careers. Not a problem, probably not going off the mountain, but bottom-row guys." 6th Row: Kyler MurrayMinnesota Vikings Tyler HuntleyBaltimore Ravens Sam DarnoldSeattle Seahawks Tyler ShoughNew Orleans Saints Jalon DanielsTampa Bay Buccaneers Jayden DanielsWashington Commanders Wright: "Sixth row, fair is fair, move them up. Kyler finally got a little juice in that offense — nice touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson, looked good for his first time in a Vikings uniform. He moves up. Tyler Huntley, maybe he needs to take the mantle as the best backup quarterback in the league. They went about half the games with him, and they didn’t look like a knee-capped operation that had no chance of moving the ball. He moves up. "Sam Darnold has not looked great yet this year, and the benefit of the doubt he’s built up is shrinking just a bit. He drops. Tyler Shough — maybe it turns out a lot of the optimism was from playing the Lions, and playing Detroit can do a lot for whoever’s on the other side. "Shout out to Jalon Daniels for Thursday night and Jalon Daniels' delightful interview with his mother that I liked a lot. "Jayden Daniels is back on the mountain because you're healthy again. The stuff you did with your legs in this game was actually really dynamic, and there were a lot of positive moments. I can't get over the ending. I understand. All probably David Blough's fault. I like my quarterbacks to have you know an idea of what quarter it is, what the rules are, if you have timeouts." 5th Row: Drake MayeNew England Patriots Aaron RodgersPittsburgh Steelers C.J. StroudHouston Texans Michael Penix JR.Atlanta Falcons Kirk CousinsLas Vegas Raiders Wright: "Look at Drake Maye — back in, back. That’s the steady climb back up the mountain. He almost got row four after a five-touchdown performance. Aaron Rodgers is playing really well — fair is fair, two of his last three games, he’s been excellent. C.J. Stroud stays where he is, even though they finally got a win. It took three quarters against the Titans, but he’s been consistent all year, playing really well. "Penix got hit in the ribs — I don’t know if he’ll miss time, so he’s not off the mountain for injury, but after a shaky early part of that game I thought he looked really sharp against Baltimore. And Kirk Cousins falls to the fifth row. Feels fair." 4th Row: Bryce YoungCarolina Panthers Matthew StaffordLos Angeles Rams Dak PrescottDallas Cowboys Jordan LoveGreen Bay Packers Wright: "Fourth row — Bryce had a bye week, so he stays where he is. Stafford moved up in a loss — I thought Stafford was really good. Dak moves down after an awful Thursday Night Football performance — well, he wasn’t awful, but he wasn’t great. "Jordan Love, holy moly, how about that possession — chucking it deep, offensive pass interference, chucking it deep again, dropped, doing it again, touchdown. Jordan Love looked really good. He moves up." 3rd Row: Trevor LawrenceJacksonville Jaguars Josh AllenBuffalo Bills Joe BurrowCincinnati Bengals Wright: "The prince made it onto the ballot but drops on the mountain. I didn’t think Trevor (Lawrence) was great in that game — the fourth-and-five throw to Parker Washington was awesome, an unbelievable catch, but there’s no shame in being on row three. "Look who he’s with: Josh Allen, who, despite only completing 12 passes, was dynamic in the fourth quarter and overtime and deadly with his legs all game, and Joe Burrow. An interesting year where he hasn’t made terrible mistakes and has obviously been good, but by his standards the numbers are just good, not great. Three of the six best plays in the NFL this season are by his receivers in the last few weeks, so Higgins and Chase are doing a lot this year. Burrow’s still great. The team’s good, not great yet." 2nd Row: Jared GoffDetroit Lions Brock PurdySan Francisco 49ers Wright: "A change in row two: Jared Goff. They’re scoring more points than anyone in the league, they have one of the most efficient offenses ever. He's not turning the ball over. He’s been fantastic; they have to score these kinds of points. "Brock Purdy almost moved up to the top — he was brilliant late in that game. However, it was also the lowest passer rating he’s had this year, the fewest yards, and the first time he’s been intercepted this year. I thought it was not his worst performance of the year, but I’d rather it be next week, when he takes the all-time passer rating lead." 1st Row: Patrick MahomesKansas City Chiefs Wright: "Still atop the mountain, because unlike Brock Purdy, he was not intercepted this week. articles.title: Broncos QB Bo Nix Explains Why Playing 'Good' Or 'Bad' Is A 'Made-Up Narrative'
articles.summary: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix pushed back on the "narrative" that he's having a bad season.
articles.body: One might argue that Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has been underwhelming this season, compared to his play in previous years. But Nix is not among those people. "I think playing good and playing bad, it’s all a narrative and I think it’s honestly kind of something we make up," Nix said at Broncos practice Tuesday. "I don’t necessarily think I’m playing any different than what I’m normally playing. … I'm confident in my preparation. I'm confident in my coaching, and I'm confident in our offense and the way we're going to structure the game and call plays." Through Denver's first five games, Nix has totaled 942 passing yards, six passing touchdowns, three interceptions and an 80.8 passer rating, while completing 59.9% of his passes. The quarterback's passer rating and completion percentage are each career lows. Last season (2025), Nix logged 3,931 passing yards, 25 passing touchdowns, 11 interceptions and an 87.8 passer rating, while completing 63.4% of his passes. The year prior (2024), Nix threw for 29 touchdowns, posted a 93.3 passer rating and completed 66.3% of his passes. He also rushed for 393.0 yards and 4.5 touchdowns per year from 2024-25. In the Broncos' Week 5 road win over the Los Angeles Chargers, Nix threw for just 123 yards. Granted, the Broncos, who won 14 games and reached the AFC Championship Game last season, are still 3-2. "It’s a mental battle, and that’s kind of where I find myself sometimes in a season like this where it’s not as good as you want it to look, but you’re winning, and you’re playing tough teams, and you’ve gotten close against a few more tough teams," Nix expressed. Denver's offense is 30th in the NFL in total yards (269.0 per game), 26th in points (19.4 per game) and 25th in both passing yards (182.8 per game) and rushing yards (86.2 per game). The Broncos changed offensive playcallers last week, with head coach Sean Payton taking the duties back from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, who was a first-time playcaller and promoted to offensive coordinator in the offseason. Last season (2025), Denver's offense was 10th in the NFL in total yards (342.6 per game) and 14th in points (23.6 per game). Of course, this came against the backdrop of the Broncos' defense leading the sport in sacks (68.0), while being second in opponent total yards (278.2 per game) and third in opponent points (18.3 per game). Like its offense, Denver's defense has regressed in production this season, as the Broncos are 29th in opponent rushing yards (145.2 per game), 22nd in opponent total yards (347.4 per game), 13th in opponent points (22.2 per game), ninth outright in opponent passing yards (202.2 per game) and tied for ninth in sacks (13.0). "I think sometimes I can have a tendency of overanalyzing things and overthinking things, and that’s when I’m not at my best," Nix said. "I want to have all the answers and get everything right, and it’s just too difficult." Nix also expressed that he can't be "worried about throwing an interception." Rather, he needs to "just play the play." Nix and the Broncos have a prime-time showdown at home against the defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night.

articles.title: Paro nacional en Bogotá hoy: puntos de marchas, movilidad y TransMilenio
articles.standfirst: Manifestaciones hoy en Bogotá: vías cerradas, desvíos y estado del tráfico
articles.summary: Manifestaciones hoy en Bogotá: vías cerradas, desvíos y estado del tráfico
articles.body: Este miércoles 14 de octubre de 2026, la ciudad de Bogotá enfrenta una jornada de alta complejidad en materia de movilidad y espacio público debido a la realización de cerca de 18 convocatorias de marchas, plantones y movilizaciones en el marco del Paro Nacional. Sindicalistas, colectivos estudiantiles, organizaciones indígenas, ambientales y sectores sociales se han dado cita en distintos puntos de la capital para marchar, en su gran mayoría, hacia la Plaza de Bolívar. La Administración Distrital, a través de la Secretaría de Movilidad, la Secretaría de Gobierno y TransMilenio, ha desplegado operativos especiales y equipos de Diálogo Social para acompañar la jornada y mitigar el impacto en los desplazamientos de los ciudadanos. Las movilizaciones se han activado de manera escalonada desde las primeras horas de la mañana, afectando importantes corredores viales en diversas localidades: Las autoridades distritales han reportado diversas novedades operativas y bloqueos intermitentes a lo largo del día: Carrera Séptima: Las marchas a la altura del Parque Nacional han obligado a la implementación de desvíos preventivos para los servicios duales y zonales de TransMilenio, generando congestión vehicular en calzadas mixtas. Las rutas alternas recomendadas incluyen la Avenida Circunvalar y la NQS. Calle 13 (Avenida Centenario): En el sector occidental (carrera 123 y cercanías de la 104), las manifestaciones ajenas a la operación de transporte han generado afectaciones intermitentes en ambos sentidos, impactando a miles de usuarios de rutas zonales. Centro de Bogotá: Como medida preventiva de alistamiento ante la llegada masiva de manifestantes a la Plaza de Bolívar, se dispusieron cierres viales en la carrera Octava entre calles 13 y 6. Colegios públicos: Por su parte, la Secretaría de Educación confirmó que las clases en los colegios oficiales de la ciudad se desarrollan con normalidad este miércoles. articles.title: Packers Star Micah Parsons Explains Why He Doesn't 'Need Revenge' Vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Even if he was active, Packers superstar Micah Parsons explained why he doesn't "need revenge" against the Cowboys, his old team.
articles.body: One might think that Green Bay Packers superstar defensive end Micah Parsons will miss out on the chance to get revenge against the Dallas Cowboys when the two teams square off at Lambeau Field in Week 6, as Parsons continues to recover from a torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of last season; Parsons had an ugly contract dispute with the Cowboys last year that led to them trading him to the Packers. But Parsons doesn't see it that way. "So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on the latest episode of his podcast, "The Edge with Micah Parsons." "It's just another Sunday Night Football game against two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's going to want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just wanna be healthy again. That's it. I don’t care about the team I left or the team they think I want my revenge against. I don’t need revenge. I just need two healthy knees to do what I love to do." Parsons noted that he's "making sure" he has "all the small things fixed" before returning to play. Green Bay acquired Parsons from Dallas within two weeks of the 2025 NFL regular season, sending defensive tackle and three-time Pro Bowler Kenny Clark and its 2026 and 2027 first-round picks to the Cowboys for the superstar defender. Parsons then signed a four-year, $186 million extension with the Packers. The two teams have already played each other since the blockbuster trade, as the Packers and Cowboys played to a 40-40 tie in Week 4 of last season in Dallas. Parsons logged one sack and three combined tackles in the contest. In the 14 games Parsons played with the Packers last year before tearing his ACL, he totaled 12.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and 41.0 combined tackles, earning his third All-Pro honor and fifth Pro Bowl nod. Without Parsons, the Packers' defense is fifth in the NFL in opponent passing yards (181.0 per game) and eighth in opponent total yards (308.6 per game). Granted, they're tied for 14th in opponent points (22.4 per game) and tied for 24th in opponent rushing yards (127.6 per game). He was a Pro Bowler in each of his four seasons with the Cowboys (2021-24) and an All-Pro in both 2021 and 2022. As for the present, the Packers are 3-2 and coming off a 31-7 victory at home over the Chicago Bears, while the Cowboys are 2-3 and coming off a 24-16 loss at home to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

articles.title: 'El Pibe' Valderrama se rapó por competo y se despidió de su icónica melena
articles.standfirst: El radical cambio de look del Pibe Valderrama y este es su nuevo aspecto
articles.summary: El radical cambio de look del Pibe Valderrama y este es su nuevo aspecto
articles.body: El fútbol sudamericano y los millones de fanáticos que crecieron admirando la magia del histórico 10 de la selección Colombia vivieron un momento insólito y difícil de imaginar: Carlos El Pibe Valderrama decidió raparse por completo, dejando atrás la melena rizada que lo acompañó durante décadas y que se convirtió en todo un símbolo cultural del deporte. A sus 65 años, el legendario mediocampista samario compartió a través de sus redes sociales un video en el que muestra el radical cambio de look. La transformación, realizada con la ayuda de su esposa Elvira Redondo, desató una ola inmediata de reacciones y comentarios en el mundo digital. En el metraje compartido por el propio exjugador, se puede observar el proceso en el que su cabellera rizada desaparece bajo la máquina de afeitar. Entre risas y un tono jocoso, la pareja bromeó sobre el impacto que tendría la nueva apariencia, llegando a especular incluso si sus propios nietos lograrían reconocerlo sin sus característicos rizos. Al verse frente al espejo con su nueva imagen, el histórico capitán del combinado nacional se mostró satisfecho y cerró el momento con su tradicional carisma y una frase muy costeña: “Joda, se quedó bacano”. La publicación revolucionó las redes sociales en cuestión de horas. Excompañeros de profesión, figuras del entretenimiento y seguidores de distintas generaciones no tardaron en manifestar su asombro. “Pibete, el que es lindo es lindo. Te quedó chevere”, escribió su amigo René Higuita. Personalidades de la música como el cantautor colombiano Santiago Cruz expresaron su cariño hacia la leyenda con mensajes de admiración: "El que es bello es bello, el que es leyenda es leyenda. Abrazo, jefe adorado", escribió. Sin embargo, el impacto fue tal que en las plataformas digitales muchos internautas comenzaron a dudar de la autenticidad de las imágenes, preguntándose si se trataba de una broma o de un montaje generado por inteligencia artificial, aunque hasta el momento el video se mantiene en sus canales oficiales como un hecho real. La cabellera rubia de El Pibe Valderrama trascendió largamente el ámbito estético. Durante las décadas de los ochenta y noventa, sus rizos dorados brillaron en las canchas de todo el mundo, convirtiéndose en el acompañamiento perfecto para su magistral visión de juego, su calidad técnica y su liderazgo inconfundible en los mundiales de Italia 1990, Estados Unidos 1994 y Francia 1998. Para varias generaciones de colombianos, la silueta de Valderrama con su abundante melena era tan reconocible como la camiseta de la selección. Aunque por ahora no se ha confirmado si este cambio responde a una campaña publicitaria o a un proyecto personal, lo cierto es que el "10" ha vuelto a sacudir las tendencias, demostrando que, con o sin rizos, su estatus de leyenda sigue intacto.

articles.title: Las sanciones que pueden caerle a Sencia por el mal estado de la grama en el Campín
articles.standfirst: Alcaldía e IDRD evalúan sanciones a Sencia por el mal estado de la gramilla de El Campín
articles.summary: Alcaldía e IDRD evalúan sanciones a Sencia por el mal estado de la gramilla de El Campín
articles.body: El estado actual del terreno de juego del Estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín desató una crisis institucional y deportiva en la capital del país. Siguiendo directrices del alcalde mayor, Carlos Fernando Galán, el Instituto Distrital de Recreación y Deporte (IDRD) puso en marcha los mecanismos contractuales para evaluar posibles sanciones e incumplimientos por parte de Sencia, el concesionario a cargo del escenario. La gota que derramó el vaso fue la cancelación del compromiso entre Millonarios y Once Caldas, un hecho que evidenció graves problemas en la adherencia y fijación de la nueva grama tras los recientes procesos de retiro y reinstalación del césped. A través de sus redes sociales, el alcalde Carlos Fernando Galán fue categórico al referirse a la situación: “Las condiciones de la grama del Campín son inaceptables. Le pido al IDRD que se inicie un proceso por posible incumplimiento de Sencia, en lo relativo a la obligación de mantener la grama del estadio en óptimas condiciones para garantizar la realización de los partidos de fútbol. No admitiremos más excusas por parte del concesionario, esta es una obligación de resultado con la cual deben cumplir”. Por su parte, el director del IDRD, Daniel García Cañón, respaldó la postura del mandatario local y recordó que el capítulo 12 del contrato de concesión contempla herramientas jurídicas estrictas frente a fallas de esta magnitud, tales como descuentos asociados a indicadores de calidad, multas severas y la aplicación de la cláusula penal. “La prioridad del estadio El Campín es el fútbol, por encima de los espectáculos. No podemos aceptar que un jugador se lesione por las condiciones del campo de juego, ni que los hinchas lleguen al estadio y encuentren la grama en este estado”, aseveró García Cañón, quien también destacó que desde febrero de este año se modificó el contrato para incorporar un manual específico de operación y mantenimiento enfocado en el seguimiento al césped. De acuerdo con el reporte de la interventoría técnica —encabezada por Harold Huertas—, los inconvenientes se originaron tras una serie de trabajos de recuperación en los que se detectaron altos niveles de humedad en algunas zonas del campo, impidiendo que el césped se fijara de manera adecuada. Aunque Sencia entregó un cronograma a finales de septiembre, las fallas físicas del terreno terminaron por impedir la práctica del balompié profesional. Ante este panorama crítico, el Distrito anunció que solicitará al concesionario revisar y reevaluar la realización de los próximos espectáculos musicales programados en el escenario para los días 24 y 31 de octubre, con el único objetivo de liberar fechas que permitan la óptima recuperación de la cancha. Desde el IDRD se reiteró que, si bien la administración comercial y de espectáculos recae sobre el concesionario, los riesgos operativas y de mantenimiento son de su absoluta competencia. Asimismo, se recordó que el estadio Metropolitano de Techo se mantiene como una alternativa coordinada con los clubes deportivos locales para garantizar que los equipos de la capital sigan compitiendo en su ciudad. El Distrito continuará vigilando de cerca los informes de la interventoría independiente y exigirá un plan de contingencia detallado a Sencia. La consigna de la administración es clara: garantizar la seguridad de los futbolistas y devolverle a la hinchada bogotana un gramado a la altura de la historia de El Campín.

articles.title: Roll The Tape: Why The Eagles' New Offense Is A Bad Fit For QB Jalen Hurts
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 5, Bucky Brooks examines four new developments to watch.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles are struggling like never before with QB Jalen Hurts. The Denver Broncos' offense isn't any better. Former blue-chip wide receiver prospect Marvin Harrison Jr. has a new team. The New York Jets have a new star defender. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are four developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.Philly's Offense Is Broken And There's No Easy Fix It is rare for a Super Bowl MVP to land on the hot seat shortly after feeling the confetti fall on his shoulders, but Philly natives are growing restless after watching the Eagles’ offense sputter and stall again under Jalen Hurts. The perennial title contenders are sitting at 2-3, with an offense that ranks near the bottom of the league in most major statistical categories. The Eagles’ anemic running game is accompanied by a scattershot aerial attack that doesn’t appear to have any rhyme or reason under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. To be fair, the Eagles are dealing with numerous personnel issues, from injuries (Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith) to departures (A.J. Brown, Lane Johnson, Cam Jurgens) that have wrecked an offensive lineup built to overwhelm opponents with superior talent. Now, Hurts is overseeing a patchwork offense that lacks the star power to roll over opponents, while being asked to do more in a traditional scheme that wants him to operate like a pass-first point guard instead of a playmaker who scores in multiple ways. Without an elite wideout on the perimeter, Hurts is expected to get it done with a wide receiver-by-committee approach that features a borderline WR1 (Smith) and a collection of B-list pass catchers (Hollywood Brown, Dontavyion Wicks, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper) who don’t scare opposing defensive coordinators or defenders with their individual or collective talents. Although some Eagles’ supporters might dispute that sentiment based on the first-round pedigrees of Brown and Lemon, neither has made an impact in Philly that demands attention from their opponents thus far. Until they are able to spark the offense with splash plays, the Eagles will rely heavily on Smith and Dallas Goedert as Wicks makes key contributions in a supporting role. While the Eagles have succeeded without a marquee pass-catcher in the past (see: 2017), the lack of five-star perimeter talents puts more pressure on the offensive line and running game to produce results to help the quarterback find positive plays down the field. Barkley has been a non-factor this season due to injuries limiting the bulk of his work to two games (Washington and Chicago). Despite averaging 5.1 yards per carry in those contests, his absence and the losses of Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley have forced the Eagles into a one-dimensional attack that was doomed from the start. In that past, the Eagles’ stellar offensive line could mask their playmakers’ woes because they could dominate the line of scrimmage and allow marginal backs to churn out yards between the tackles. However, the loss of respected offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland and the aforementioned departures of Jurgens and Johnson, leaves the Eagles searching for an identity within the trenches with a bunch of newcomers trying to figure it out in a new system. Speaking of schematics, the addition of Mannion as the offensive coordinator also appears to be a poor fit based on his preferred system and Hurts’ abilities. Mannion, of course, is the fifth OC head coach Nick Sirianni has hired in his six-year joint tenure with Hurts. While the Sean McVay/Matt LaFleur disciple brings over Xs and Os that have helped several quarterbacks flourish in the pocket, Mannion's traditional dropbacks and play-action concepts from shotgun and under center are a far cry from the RPO (run-pass option) concepts that helped turn Hurts into an unstoppable force as the Eagles’ QB1. Although the franchise quarterback should be able to adapt and adjust to a new playbook as an experienced starter with a 59-28 career record, the tactics don’t mesh well with his talent, so his 2026 struggles are not surprising. Watching the Eagles’ operation in Week 5, the disconnect between Hurts and the rest of the offense is startling. From the stagnant ground attack due to lackluster runners plunging into clogged holes, to the "dink-and-dunk" throws to covered receivers, the Eagles’ lack the personnel and playbook to challenge heavyweight opponents right now. Perhaps more time on task and the return of their frontline stars can help revive Philly into a title contender, but the offense’s struggles are destined to continue until Hurts is put in an offense that leans more into his playmaking rather than exposes his flaws as a passer. 2.How Broncos HC Sean Payton Will Try To Rejuvenate QB Bo Nix After watching his offense sputter under new offensive coordinator Davis Webb, Broncos head coach Sean Payton snatched the call sheet from the former NFL journeyman QB to help Bo Nix and Co. find the balance and rhythm that has been missing in 2026. Despite promising to stay out of the way of the first-time playcaller, Payton stepped in to keep the Broncos from missing a potential Super Bowl run while Davis finishes his on-the-job training. With the Broncos ranking 26th in scoring offense and Nix playing the worst ball of his career, the offensive wizard needed to take the call sheet back to help a promising young quarterback rediscover the magic that helped him lead 10 game-winning drives over his first two seasons, while completing 64.8% of his passes with a 54:23 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Most importantly, Nix led the Broncos to back-to-back playoff appearances and last season's AFC Championship Game thanks to his steady play under Payton. Part of his success as a young QB can be attributed to Payton's conservative approach, which eased the pressure on the former first-rounder. The offense blended a movement-based passing game with a diverse running game to keep opponents from attacking Nix with exotic pressures from every angle. Although the Broncos lacked a premier running back in the backfield, their rotation forced opponents to prepare for a creative running game that featured role-playing specialists (Javonte Williams, Jaleel McLaughlin, J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey) anchoring a mid-ranking running game that was just good enough to keep opponents from loading up against an efficient aerial attack. Stretch zone runs and complementary bootlegs, plus the inside run and various RPO combinations, allowed Nix to maximize his playmaking potential as an athletic passer with plus-running skills. Nix’s impromptu scrambles and occasional designed runs added another dimension to the offense as Payton sought to build a ball-control unit that complemented a disruptive defense. In Week 5, the Broncos returned to a complementary game, with Payton balancing the call log to feature a 50-50 run-pass ratio. The Broncos ran 29 times and passed 27, while capitalizing on the prime scoring opportunities the defense created. Although the stat sheet was far from impressive, with the team amassing just 224 net yards and Nix finishing with the second-lowest passing output of his career (123 yards), the offense’s flow matched his strengths as a "game manager" with a keen understanding of how to play winning football (avoiding sacks and turnovers) for a playoff contender. While Payton must find more ways to incorporate wideouts Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton into the game plan to increase the offense’s explosive potential, he must do it while rebuilding Nix’s confidence with high-completion throws and "chain-moving" plays that keep the offense on schedule. With Nix also thriving in "tempo" situations at the end of games, the Broncos could mix in some no-huddle to help the young quarterback face more vanilla defensive looks that allow him to operate in attack mode from the pocket. After taking back the call sheet to help his franchise quarterback and offense get back on track, Payton must continue to take bold measures to get the Broncos back to playing the efficient brand of ball that has made them title contenders under his direction. 3.How WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Can Rebound In Houston Is one's trash another's treasure? That's what the Texans are betting on after acquiring once-ballyhooed Ohio State standout Marvin Harrison Jr. and reuniting him with quarterback C.J. Stroud. Although the football world has seemingly soured on MHJ after posting 1,578 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns in 33 career games, the third-year pro needed a winning organization with a demanding culture to get back on track after an up-and-down journey with the Cardinals. The Texans’ impressive track record of turning top picks into stars (see: Stroud, OLB Will Anderson and CB Derek Stingley) bodes well for the 6-foot-3, 220-pound Harrison, who flashed elite receiving skills before falling out of favor amid a slump that exposed his flaws as a playmaker. Harrison’s inability to separate against bump-and-run and tight coverage led to too many 50-50 balls for a big-bodied pass catcher expected to anchor the passing game like Larry Fitzgerald once did in Arizona. With MHJ's effort and concentration waning near the end of his tenure, the Texans are hoping a change of scenery, a new scheme and better connection with his quarterback will help the super-sized pass-catcher regain his swagger as a high-end WR2 for an offense that desperately needs a reliable threat opposite Pro Bowler Nico Collins. Studying the All-22 coaches’ footage from MHJ’s rookie season shows he entered the league with the tools to be a designated playmaker in an offense built around his game. In the second game of his career, he totaled 130 receiving yards and a pair of scores on just four catches against the Los Angeles Rams. The tape reveals a sticky-fingered receiver with outstanding balance, body control, and awareness. As a natural pass-catcher with strong hands, Harrison can climb the ladder on boundary alley-oops or post up smaller defenders on curls and in-breaking routes between the hashes. He also flashes enough speed and quickness to beat squatting defenders on vertical routes that accompany play-action or misdirection fakes in the backfield. For a Texans squad that needs a dependable weapon with big-play potential, Harrison’s revival could resurrect the team’s playoff hopes and ignite an offense that has been looking for a spark plug on the perimeter. 4.Why Jets DE David Bailey Is The Defensive ROY Front-Runner If the 2026 regular season ended today, Jets defensive end David Bailey should be the undisputed choice as the NFL’s Defensive Rookie of the Year. The No. 2 overall pick has dominated as expected as a speed-rushing phenom with exceptional first-step quickness and closing burst. Through five games, Bailey has recorded five sacks, including a hat trick against the Cleveland Browns that showcased his speed, quickness and burst around the corner. The 6-foot-3, 251-pounder posted a jaw-dropping 40-yard dash time (4.50) prior to the draft, and his explosive quickness shows up repeatedly as he blows past blockers on simple speed-rushing moves. In studying each of Bailey’s three sacks against Cleveland, the rookie standout showed he can mix force with finesse to keep blockers guessing on the edges. On his first sack, Bailey attacked rookie offensive tackle Spencer Fano with a two-handed bull rush and dog-walked the blocker into Deshaun Watson’s lap. The explosive move exploited the blocker’s fear of his speed by running through him as he waited for a "dip-and-rip" off the edge. Bailey’s second sack came from a cleverly designed blitz from a "Double Mug" (six-man front with linebackers walked up on each side of the center) front that sent Bailey off the edge, with Jarvis Brownlee shooting inside through the B-gap (space between the right tackle and right guard), creating a two-on-one matchup against OT Tytus Howard on the edge. With the veteran opting to protect the inside gap because of the quarterback's proximity, Bailey waltzed in for an easy quarterback takedown. With the Browns unsure how the rookie would attack, given his diverse repertoire of pass-rush moves, the hat trick on his patented "dip-and-rip" rush shouldn’t surprise anyone who studied his game at Stanford and Texas Tech. Bailey exploded off the edge facing OT Dawand Jones, and the veteran couldn't kick-step quick enough to stay in front of the hard-charging pass-rusher. As Jets coach Aaron Glenn continues to find fun and creative ways to deploy Bailey as a designated pass-rusher with elite playmaking skills, the football world can expect to see the rookie continually making splash plays.

articles.title: Trusty To Return To The Starting XI? | Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Benfica
articles.summary: A comfortable 2-0 win over Motherwell should put Celtic in a better place ahead of their trip to Portugal. They will lock horns with Benfica on Thursday nigh...
articles.body:
A comfortable 2-0 win over Motherwell should put Celtic in a better place ahead of their trip to Portugal. They will lock horns with Benfica on Thursday night in the Europa League , as the Hoops must bounce back after their home defeat to Ferencvárosi in the first gameweek.

But they need to punch above their weight to grab a result against the Portuguese heavyweights, who humbled AC Milan at San Siro in September. Benfica are prime contenders for the coveted trophy, and it remains to be seen how Martin O'Neill lines up Celtic to counter Marco Silva's structured style of football built on positional fluidity, high-intensity wide play, and central compactness.

Predicted 4-2-3-1 Celtic Lineup To Face Benfica

After a clean sheet at Fir Park, Viljami Sinisalo should keep his place between the sticks despite losing his spot to veteran Sam Johnstone for a couple of fixtures before the international break.

MOTHERWELL, SCOTLAND – OCTOBER 11: Haissem Hassan of Celtic battles for possession with Ibrahim Said of Motherwell during the William Hill Premiership 2026/27 match between Motherwell and Celtic at Fir Park on October 11, 2026 in Motherwell, Scotland. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images)

Colby Donovan has been preferred at right-back amid Alistair Johnston's injury absence. The young academy prodigy must get the nod over Anthony Ralston. Compatriot Cameron Carter-Vicker's fitness woes could see Auston Trusty return to the starting XI, replacing Dane Murray and partnering with Liam Scales in the heart of the backline. Kieran Tierney remains the obvious choice for the left-back spot, as his understudy Landon Emenalo has not been included in their European squad. Jordan Lotomba, primarily a right-back, might be introduced as a makeshift left-back from the bench.

Skipper Callum McGregor must step up his game to control the show from the deep. Mika Baur should focus more on marshalling the defence rather than operating in the advanced areas of the pitch. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is available for selection following a three-game suspension, and the veteran Englishman is expected to feature as a second-half substitute alongside Oliver Sørensen and Luke McCowan. Benjamin Nygren lacks work ethic but could make a difference in close contests with his creative spark and poaching traits as a 'number 10'.

Yang Hyun-Jun is sidelined with a hamstring strain, and the gaffer should opt for Camilo Duran on the left-hand flank over Sebastian Tounekti. Shifting Duran to the left would make way for Haissem Hassan, who fits better as a right-sided attacker. Fit-again Jota is not registered for Europe, leaving the Bhoys with Tounekti and James Forrest as wide attacking alternatives.

Kasper Høgh, though low in confidence, should spearhead their frontline, with Shim Mheuka loaned in only from Chelsea for the domestic competitions.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers guard Aaron Banks returns to practice Oct. 14, 3 others absent
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers were back to practice as they prepare to host the Dallas Cowboys. Veteran guard Aaron Banks returned to the field.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY − Green Bay Packers guard Aaron Banks returned to practice Oct. 14.

Banks has been dealing with knee and toe injuries since the start of the season, playing only in the first half of the Week 2 game against the New York Jets.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur confirmed he would practice on a limited basis.

The Packers have slowly been building some continuity on the interior of the offensive line with Laken Tomlinson stepping in at left guard in place of Banks and Travis Glover starting the past two games at right guard.

The Packers also have Kevin Zeitler at right guard, so it could make for an interesting decision once Banks is healthy and ready to play.

"It's going to be pretty fluid," LaFleur said. "We've got see where he's at. He hasn't practiced in a really long time. I think those other guys have come in and done a really good job."

Three other players missed practice, as the Packers prepare to host the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 18.

Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon was held out of practice.

Nixon hasn't been on the injury report and played the complete game during the Packers' Oct. 11 win over the Chicago Bears .

The first injury report will be released today to provide more clarity on his injury.

He was present and off to the side with the rest of the rehab group.

Packers cornerback Benjamin St-Juste also was out during practice.

He's been dealing with a hamstring injury throughout this season and injured it again during the Bears game.

Packers receiver and return specialist Skyy Moore did not participate in practice.

Moore suffered an ankle injury during the Bears game.

LaFleur said he doesn't anticipate it to be a long-term injury.

Packers guard Jacob Monk was dressed out and participating in practice.

Monk made his return to practice Oct. 9, but missed his second straight game due to a quadricep injury.

Packers defensive tackle Anthony Campbell was present at practice.

Campbell participated in practice all of last week, as well, but was ruled out for the third straight game after injuring his ankle during the Week 2 game against the New York Jets.

Packers receiver Savion Williams was practicing and working toward his return to game action.

Williams returned to practice Oct. 7 officially opening his 21-day practice window. He opened the season on injured reserve due to an ankle injury in preseason.

Packers defensive tackle Jordon Riley participated in practice Oct. 14 for the first time since last season.

Riley suffered a season-ending Achilles injury during the Week 17 game against the Baltimore Ravens.

He opened the season on the physically-unable-to-perform list. Riley's 21-day practice window is now open, and the Packers can decide to activate him at any time.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield gives injury update ahead of Week 6 vs Steelers
articles.summary: Buccaneers reveal latest on Mayfield's injury status.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have received an encouraging update regarding their starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield, as the team prepares for its Week 6 NFL matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Baker Mayfield "getting better," will test thumb with Wednesday throwing session. — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) October 14, 2026

Baker Mayfield "getting better," will test thumb with Wednesday throwing session.

ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) October 14, 2026

Mayfield, 31, has missed Tampa Bay's last two games after suffering a dislocated thumb. However, the veteran quarterback is reportedly getting better and is scheduled to test the injury during a throwing session on Wednesday afternoon.

Despite the progress, Mayfield is not expected to be ready for Sunday's game. The Buccaneers are taking a cautious approach with their starting quarterback as they look to ensure he fully recovers before returning to the field.

Sep 27, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) scrambles with the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images

Mayfield appeared in Tampa Bay's first three games of the season before sustaining the thumb injury. During that stretch, he threw for 615 yards and two touchdowns, although the Buccaneers lost all three contests.

The quarterback is in his fourth season with Tampa Bay after establishing himself as a key part of the franchise's offense. Last season, he recorded more than 3,600 passing yards and 26 touchdown passes while adding 382 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown across 17 games.

His absence has forced Tampa Bay to turn to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who has started the team's last two games.

Daniels delivered an encouraging performance in Week 5, throwing for 189 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers' 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The win provided Tampa Bay with a much-needed boost as the team navigates its quarterback situation.

Sep 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) makes a pass during the second quarter at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images

Although Mayfield is making progress, the Buccaneers do not appear willing to rush him back into action before he is fully healthy. He is unlikely to serve as the team's emergency backup against Pittsburgh, meaning Daniels could once again be called upon to lead the offense.

Head coach Todd Bowles emphasized the importance of ensuring Mayfield is completely recovered before returning.

"If he's not 100 percent, he doesn't need to play," Bowles said.

That approach could keep Mayfield sidelined for another week, depending on how his throwing session goes and how his thumb responds afterward.

The Buccaneers, currently 1-4, will host the 3-2 Steelers on Sunday. While Mayfield's potential return remains uncertain, Tampa Bay will hope his recovery continues progressing as the team looks to build on its Week 5 victory.

articles.title: Chris Sale and multiple Braves teammates announced as finalists for Gold Glove, MLBPA awards
articles.summary: Matt Olson should win his fourth Gold Glove, at least
articles.body:
With the MLB postseason no longer delivering frenetic news days given that we're in League Championship Series season, where there's not even two games on most days, it's time for the faux-anticipation of dropping finalists (not winners, finalists) for certain end-of-season awards.

We've got two on the docket today. First, Gold Gloves.

I have a bone to pick with Gold Gloves, as you've probably read by now. There's a way to do the whole Gold Glove thing objectively. Would it be perfect? Nah. But it would at least be steady. Instead, we have the current Rawlings award process, which is an abomination/agglomeration of multiple criteria, some of which just make no sense. For example, one criterion does involve defensive metrics, but it's an index of multiple metrics, some of which are outdated and strictly worse than others, which just dilutes the whole endeavor. It's whack. Anyway, here we go, courtesy of MLB.com :

As far as the Braves are concerned, their Gold Glove finalists are Chris Sale, Matt Olson, Michael Harris II, and Mauricio Dubon. Let's look at these in turn.

Sale is a tough one, because no one really tries to evaluate pitcher defense in a way commensurate with other positions. The only measure we have that I'm aware of is DRS, and DRS has a load of problems. By DRS, though, Sale finished fourth in defensive value in the National League. (Foster Griffin was also ahead of him but was traded to the other league midseason.) I don't know what to do with this one. The other finalists are Michael McGreevy and Nolan McLean, who finished first and third ahead of Sale, respectively, so… I dunno, give this to McGreevy? What a weird award.

Matt Olson should probably win his fourth Gold Glove. He led all first basemen in OAA/FRV (the Statcast-based measures), blowing away basically every first baseman in terms of converting range into outs.

Michael Harris II makes sense as a finalist, but Pete Crow-Armstrong more than doubled his FRV and has a giant lead, so…

That brings us to Mauricio Dubon. The "utility" position is a tough one to evaluate, since you have to really think about what qualifies someone to even be eligible for this position, and think about positional adjustments. Inclusive of those adjustments, the three finalists here are:

Dubon, with about half a win above average, with above-average marks at short, average marks in left, and an above-average cameo in center;

Jared Triolo, who only played about half a season and had less aggregate defensive value, playing mostly third and short in nondescript fashion; and

Ildemaro Vargas, who mostly played first and second, and didn't really impress at second.

Basically, this is a weird thing, and if these are your three finalists, it feels like Dubon should win by default. That said, since apparently Nico Hoerner (played mostly second but some short) and Bryson Stott (mostly second, some third) didn't qualify for whatever reason, Dubon really does make sense as the next-best option. (For those of you saying that Hoerner and Stott shouldn't be in the running because two positions does not a utility guy make, look at Triolo and Vargas, who pretty much played… two positions.)

In terms of snubs, there's not really anything to complain about, as the other Braves didn't really warrant any real consideration here, not even as top-three finalists in the NL.

Switching gears a bit, the MLBPA announced finalists for their peer-voted Players' Choice awards here . Of relevance to the Braves are Chris Sale (but he'll probably lose to Jacob Misiorowski) as Outstanding Pitcher in the NL, and Martin Perez as Comeback Player. The other two finalists vying with Perez are Sandy Alcantara and… honestly, this award has kind of lost all meaning. Wheeler has thrown 149-plus frames every non-shortened season going back to his partial-season absence in 2017, while Alcantara is at 170-plus the last two years. What are they coming back from? Like, yeah, Alcantara wasn't that good in 2025, but don't call it a comeback. Perez wasn't particularly good in 2026, but at least his 2025 was legitimately a partial season. I don't know, this is a weird award. How about someone like Jordan Walker, who legitimately "came back" from being awful and minors-bound the past two seasons, or Michael King, who actually missed a bunch of 2025?

Don't mind me. Get that hardware, Matt Olson.

articles.title: Sean Mannion is still having a blast despite Eagles’ struggles
articles.summary: The Eagles OC talks Jalen Hurts in the run game, second-half struggles, and more.
articles.body:
The Eagles offense took steps in the right direction on Sunday in London, but with injuries and depth issues, the group still has room to grow. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion spoke to reporters this week about their second-half struggles, what he's seen from the passing game, and explained that late-game catch by Makai Lemon.

"I think we're always looking for ways to integrate [Jalen Hurts] into the run game. Some of it's dependent on the opponent and the fronts they're giving us, the looks you're getting. But like I've said in here before, it's a unique trait that he has that makes him dangerous. Some of them are designed, some of them are kind of the off-schedule plays. I think he's had a good feel for that in terms of when to take off and run. He had some big plays early in the year, first few weeks, of using his legs in the pass game, kind of those off-schedule scrambles. So, there's a place for both of them. I think he's found a nice balance of that.

Mannion went on to say that every week present a different challenge and they're going to adjust accordingly, and this week against the Jaguars, they planned for a more pass-oriented offense. He noted that some of that was intentional, and some was just how the game played out.

"We want to be an offense that is balanced and can attack you in the run game and the pass game. Then, within the game, within the week, the opponent that you're facing, your personnel, there can be little tweaks along the way that lead to a different end result in terms of your run-pass balance."

The OC also said he didn't think that the calf injury that popped up late last week affected Hurts, and overall felt the QB was ready to play and performed well.

Mannion said that early in the game, everything is heightened being their first regular season NFL action, but as the game went on, he felt like C/G Jake Majors, C/G Willie Lampkin and T Markel Bell found their footing, communicated well, and played hard.

"That's one thing, and I say it every week, but this group really, really plays hard, especially Willie, Jake, Markel, those young guys. You can just see the ferocity they're playing with out there. That's what you appreciate about them. These are three young players that we have a ton of confidence in. They're talented. They're getting their first taste of real action. I think they're going to keep getting better. We feel good about the depth of this group while we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries."

The OC said that he felt like they did a better job last week against the Jaguars coming out of halftime, and they had some opportunities in the second-half, but need to be finishing drives. He pointed out that they did have some third down conversions, and were close on the deep throw to Dontayvion Wicks.

"I think there were some chances there that we just didn't quite capitalize on. Ultimately as a staff, I'm looking every week to put ourselves in the best position possible leaving halftime to extend those drives. I think we're closer. I know the result hasn't been what we want or what we hold ourselves to as an offense, but I felt like we were getting closer in the second half. We really just have to finish some of those drives."

Mannion was asked if Lemon was supposed to go out of bounds on his catch ahead of the Eagles final field goal on Sunday. He explained that their focus there was just to advance the ball.

"They were in a cover zero look. With that comes some leverage issues where you're inside. The primary focus there was [to] advance the ball to do our best to help the kick and then get us into the best play possible to do so and avoid a negative play. So, that was the outcome we had there. Obviously, he was caught on the outbreak right by the sideline, kind of got pushed out, but our primary focus with the call and with the execution of it was to advance the ball. With the look, that's what ended up happening. We're in an outbreak and he ends up getting pushed out."

Ultimately, the OC felt like it was a bang-bang play on the sidelined, and they were primarily focused on how to help the field goal distance.

He also revealed that Lemon was the first read on that play.

Mannion doesn't think Jalen Hurts step back in completions this year is any one thing. He noted that across the board offensively, they want to improve, and that's in the run and pass games.

"I think [Jalen Hurts] is a naturally very accurate guy, so I'm confident that those numbers will continue to improve. His comfort level grows each and every week. Getting these live game reps week after week after week, he's going to grow more and more comfortable. I think the good thing is he's been making good decisions with the ball. Obviously, we had an uptick in our pass attempts last game and I thought he made good decisions with where the ball was supposed to go. I'm confident, because he is a naturally accurate passer, that those numbers will rise.

"I feel confident this group's going to be able to move the ball. We had some nice runs earlier on in the run game. We just need to keep sustaining that. Then honestly, some of it's not necessarily a negative. You feel better about some of the other calls you have on the sheet and you get to those."

Mannion also talked about Carson Steele, noting that the RB did a phenomenal job in the preseason, and he's wearing a lot of different hats for them on the practice field.

"He's a versatile player who can do a lot of nice things for us. We're looking to use all of our guys in every way possible. So, [using Steele at fullback is] certainly something we're considering."

Mannion said that working with head coach Nick Sirianni with game management decisions has been smooth, and they had a lot of opportunities during practices to work through a lot of different scenarios.

Most of the game management scenarios are talked through during the week, and they map out decisions based on different parameters and move forward accordingly.

The OC talked about how he loves coming to work everyday and getting a chance to collaborate with staff and players as a unit to achieve the best result possible. He noted his enthusiasm and his enjoyment of the process and the work hasn't waned.

"It's been a blast. There are new challenges every day, whether it be managing injuries or whether it be managing a practice plan or traveling overseas, how does that adjust our offensive meeting schedule? But that honestly is the enjoyable part. That's why you love getting into coaching is you get to work with other great coaches, get to work with a phenomenal group of players that work their butts off, they're coachable, they want to win, they want to get better. It's a new challenge every day in this role, but it's everything I hoped it would be and it's been a blast. I am really confident that if we keep attacking each day with the right mindset, with a high level of enthusiasm, with a will to just get better bit by bit, day by day, we are going to get the results that we're after."
