articles.title: The Yankees’ five best defensive plays of 2026
articles.summary: The Yankees did, in fact, make some nice plays this season.
articles.body:
The Yankees defense has been, over the past few years, inconsistent at best. The 2024 squad, on paper, wasn't too bad, ending the year in the middle of the pack in Defensive Runs Saved (31, good for 12th in baseball) and Outs Above Average (10, good for 10th), but defensive miscues rather infamously proved their downfall in the World Series that year. The 2025 team brought in a trio of Gold Glovers in Cody Bellinger, Max Fried, and Paul Goldschmidt and shifted Jazz Chisholm back to second base, but the team still finished 13th in DRS with 30 and 18th in OAA with -7. Considering the fact that, in many ways, the 2026 team ran back the 2025 version, it shouldn't come as too much of a surprise that the team once again finished 13th in DRS with 26 and 17th in OAA with -5.

As befits a team whose sum total defensively trends towards mediocrity, the Yankees had more than their fair share of highlights and lowlights this year. Today, we take a look at the team's best webgems (we'll review the misplays later this week). We're not ranking them, because defensive excellence need not be ranked, but feel free to do so in the comments section below!

Before Knicks star OG Anunoby tipped the ball into the hoop to give the Knicks the lead with 1.2 seconds left in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, you had Cody Bellinger. Okay, okay, nothing quite compares to that play, but nonetheless, the Yankees left fielder made quite a grab during the Yankees' home opener back on April 3rd. In the top of the ninth, Marlins second baseman Xavier Edwards drove a fly ball to deep left field. Ranging backwards, Bellinger leapt as the ball sailed over his head, and had he come down with it, that play would have ended up on the Honorable Mentions in this list. But he did not come down with it: he mistimed the jump, the ball hit his wrist. As the ball fell to the ground, he made a desperate stab at it…and somehow, he caught it.

I mean, just look at that face. That is a guy thinking, "Wow, I can't believe that actually worked."

We could honestly just fill this entire post with Bellinger highlights, but for the sake of, well, remembering players not named Cody Bellinger, we'll limit it to just two — or rather, to two categories, because here, I just can't pick between these two plays, both of which involve Bellinger using his arm to throw out a runner.

During the critical series between the Yankees and Red Sox at the end of August, the Yankees held a 1-0 lead late in the game. With a pair of runners in scoring position and only one away against fireman Paul Blackburn, Boston was threatening, when Willson Contreras hit a fly ball to left field for the second out of the inning. Looking to make something happen, the speedy Ceddanne Rafaela tagged up and challenged Belli, strength against strength, to make a play. He answered the call, delivering a strike to Austin Wells, as the Yankees wound up winning 1-0.

In a much less-intense version of the famous play in which Bellinger retired Juan Soto and doubled up Francisco Lindor last year, No. 35 recognized that he had a shot to double up Victor Mesa Jr., who was running on the play, and end the inning. It wasn't his best throw to first, but Luis García Jr. made a neat scoop-and-tag while falling to the ground, finishing off a beautiful 7-3 double play with style.

While only Max Fried is truly known for his defense, the Yankees pitching staff put together quite the highlight reel, so once again, I am cheating a little bit, because I can't pick just one (hey, I make the rules).

To begin, back on April 28th, Fernando Cruz slid to field a bunt off the bat of Joc Pederson, then threw to Ryan McMahon from his rear end to nab the lead runner for the first out of the inning (the play would be challenged, unsuccessfully, by the Rangers).

Just two weeks later, just one inning after being hit in the foot by a line drive, Cam Schlittler fielded a slow chopper off the bat of Mark Vientos and made an off-balance throw to fellow Massachusetts native Ben Rice for the third out of the inning against the Mets.

On June 22nd, Ryan Yarbrough took matters into his own hands and made a diving tag on a bunt.

And on September 11th, Brent Headrick escaped a bases loaded jam by catching a line drive right back up the middle off the bat of Francisco Lindor.

After he made his Major League debut at the beginning of August, George Lombard Jr. made fans throughout the Yankees fandom with his slick play at shortstop. My personal favorite? This barehanded grab on August 11th, where he fielded a ricochet off the second base bag cleanly before throwing to first for the third out of the inning.

He's Here! He's There! He's Every-Bleepin-Where!

José Caballero was the Yankees' Swiss Army knife this season. He began the year as the starting shortstop (where he played 70 games), before bouncing around the field, making 23 appearances at the keystone, 37 at the hot corner, and 22 games across all three outfield positions. And while he wasn't exactly equally proficient with the glove everywhere he played — he had 13 DRS at shortstop, 1 apiece at second and third, and -3 in the outfield — he wasn't unplayable anywhere, and made more than his fair share of highlights there.

Let's go around the diamond. Playing second base on July 24th, he made a diving stop ranging to his right to rob a base hit from Alec Bohm.

At shortstop, here's a nifty play he made on September 2nd — while not the flashiest, those in-between, not quite a line drive, not quite a ground ball ones are some of the hardest to field.

At the hot corner, he teamed up with Lombard for rather unusual 6-5-3 double play. It's the type of play that could only happen because of the shift — and because Cabby's positional versatility allows him to adapt to unusual situations.

And lastly, on June 17th, he made this diving catch against the Tigers while in left field — a play that had me worried for a second when I saw it live, as Cabby took a second to get up.

The Martian Makes the Grab, But Exits with a Concussion

articles.title: 49ers rookie report: The long-term upside is there for this class
articles.summary: Checking in on the 49ers rookie class through 5 games
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have relied on rookies to play at a high level this season. So far, they have not disappointed. There will be inevitable growing pains. That's par for the course when you're talking about first-year players.

But this draft class looks to have a few hits and potential long-term starters. Here is our rookie report after five weeks.

We're probably still another month and a half away from seeing Stribling, at the earliest. It's a bummer, because you could see the impact he could make during the preseason.

All is not lost, though. He'll have the final month of the season to work himself back into the offense. Ideally, Stribling is up to speed and a regular contributor by the playoffs.

Height was drafted to be the designated pass rusher. So far, he's rushed the passer on 62% of his snaps. We haven't seen him kick inside often, as 88% of his snaps have come on the edge.

Height has only three solo tackles on the season, with a modest pressure rate of 7.2%. He's essentially a designated looper. Per Sumer Sports, 52% of Height's pass rushes have been stunts. Raheem Morris has his rookie on the move on over half his pass-rushing snaps. He's winning at a high clip, 13.3%. That's a good sign, and it suggests Height's production should follow shortly.

The 49ers rookie running back has been underwhelming to begin the year. It looked like he'd be a focal point of the offense in Week 1, but his snaps have dwindled since. He's only playing about 11% of the time this year. Black has an explosive play rate of 2.6% and a -0.10 EPA per touch, with one impact play in his name.

Black was seen as one of the better pass-blocking prospects in the draft, but he's only been used 1.3% of the time in that role.

Kyle Shanahan isn't tipping his hand when Black is in the game. The split is pretty even: he runs the ball 47% of the time and runs a pass route 41% of the time.

Black's averaging 2.6 yards per carry in the red zone. That jumps to 3.9 yards per carry on non-red-zone carries. The good news is he's bouncing off tackles, falling forward, and gaining yards after the contact. But he's also getting stuffed behind the line of scrimmage and failing to force missed tackles.

Black struggles to resist the urge to bounce runs that don't need to or to stop his feet in the backfield. In 1-on-1 situations, he's indecisive instead of being the aggressor.

Halton recorded his first sack of the season, but he's 26th among all defensive tackles in the NFL in impact plays, with 13. He has one less impact play than Osa Odighizuwa, despite playing 91 fewer snaps. Halton has as many tackles for loss as DeForest Buckner and Zach Allen.

Halton's awareness is off the charts. He's a much better run defender than anticipated. He's the type of player who causes chaos, and his plays don't always show up in the box score.

Nothing about Halton's first five games would tell you he should've fallen to Day 3 of the draft.

Dugger only has one missed tackle this year. He also got into the sack column for the first time last week. Dugger has been sneaky good as a pass rusher. He's only rushed ten times, but he has three pressures and the sack we saw on the first drive of Week 5.

It's been impressive to watch Dugger hold his own against 300-pounders. Four of his seven targets have resulted in first downs, but he's only surrendering 6.4 yards per reception on those. Week 5 showed that some of those were by design, essentially conceding underneath throws to take away the bigger threat.

Dugger plays physically, stays in control, and rarely makes mistakes. His long-term upside is high, especially with Fred Warner at the position.

articles.title: KC Concepcion back on field for Browns as injuries pile up
articles.summary: The Browns are dealing with a rash of injuries as they prepare to face the Ravens in an AFC North showdown. They did have one key piece on the field.
articles.body:
BEREA ― The stakes in the Browns' game this week against the Baltimore Ravens are big. So, too, are the list of their players who are currently battling through injuries of different extents.

How much will those injuries ultimately come into play on Oct. 18? Browns coach Todd Monken isn't ready to say just yet.

"Well, we'll see," Monken said. "I mean, we're not going to rule anybody in or out today, but we've got a number of guys dealing with some minor issues. We'll see today and the rest of the week."

Cleveland Browns vs New York Jets: Best photos from Week 5 NFL game

The Browns had eight players off their active rosters who didn't practice Oct. 14. That included three of their top four defensive tackles ― Maliek Collins (foot), Mason Graham (knee/ankle) and Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) ― along with running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) and right tackle Tytus Howard (knee).

Graham and Hall had missed the Jets game due to their injuries, which were sustained in the previous week's win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Collins, Judkins, Schwesinger and Howard all sustained their injuries against the Jets.

Two other players, tight end Carsen Ryan (calf) and guard Teven Jenkins (back), were also out. Ryan has been sidelined since Oct. 8, while Jenkins has been out since Sept. 7.

"We'll adjust today," Monken said. "There'll be a little more walkthrough in certain periods today that we have to do. We won't have the numbers with the availability of our team. We still have to get full speed work in certain areas and we will do that."

Howard and Ryan were on the field watching practice. The others were in the facility getting treatment.

One Browns player who was on the field and practicing wide receiver KC Concepcion Jr.. The rookie sustained a concussion after being hit by New York Jets safety Minkah Fizpatrick with 4:59 remaining in the first quarter of the Browns' Week 5 loss three days earlier.

Concepcion remains in the concussion protocol. but practice is a significant step necessary in order for him to be cleared. Considering the hit and the initial aftermath, with Concecpion being on the ground with his eyes rolling back in his head, the fact he was on the field was a major step.

"No, just from a player's health perspective," Monken said, "it's cool that it wasn't worse than it was. And so that's probably the biggest thing from a health standpoint."

Clearing the protocol and playing against the Ravens isn't a certainty. If Concepcion can't go, then it likely puts more on the plates of Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond, as well as Tylan Wallace, who returned to practice after missing two games with a knee injury.

Jeudy did have two big catches on the game-winning drive against Pittsburgh. Bond had three catches for 74 yards against the Jets, but also two big drops among his seven targets.

"I mean, we hope to have KC back, but all the guys are doing a great job of just trying to learn every position," quarterback Deshaun Watson said Oct. 14. "You never know who's going to go down depending on the week and how the flow of the game is going to go. But if we all can just be on the same page and know the full game plan and not just one position, then it definitely presents itself better."

One other player who was on the field but not practicing was running back Dylan Sampson. Sampson was designated for return from the injured reserve list, which he's been on since Sept. 15.

Sampson didn't do anything on the field during practice. Beforehand, Monken merely said of the running back's chances to play against the Ravens, "I think there's a chance. He'll be out there today, and we're excited that his window has been opened."

articles.title: Chargers rumors: ESPN insider offers up defiant fantasy football advice with potential LA fire sale on horizon
articles.summary: With the Los Angeles Chargers starting 0-5 on the season and the offense down in the dumps, there could still be some valuable fantasy football usage to take...
articles.body:
With the Los Angeles Chargers starting 0-5 on the season and the offense down in the dumps, there could still be some valuable fantasy football usage to take advantage of with the team. As the Chargers take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6 , this NFL insider has some fantasy football advice when it comes to the team's running backs.

A popular draft-day pick for fantasy football managers was running back Omarion Hampton , and while Keaton Mitchell is the player behind him, league insider Dan Graziano says Kimani Vidal is "emerging as a real factor" for Los Angeles. While seeing little to no usage in the first three weeks, it progressed to five and eight carries in Weeks 4 and 5.

"He [Vidal] didn't have a carry or a target in either of the Chargers' first two games of the season, and he had one carry and three targets in Week 3. But over the last two weeks, Vidal has carried the ball 13 times for 82 yards and been targeted five times in the passing game. Over that same time, Omarion Hampton has 23 carries for 78 yards and three targets while Keaton Mitchell has 16 carries for 50 yards and 10 targets," Graziano wrote.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Chargers "could start unloading players soon"

While Graziano gets the wariness of someone from taking a player from the slumping Chargers, the insider would say that the team "could start unloading players soon," which could make Vidal's opportunity continue to go up, no matter his situation.

"Running back is a tough position in fantasy, and Vidal had success last year when thrust into the feature back role and is now taking on a larger role for a 0-5 team searching for any answers it can find," Graziano wrote. "There are worse fliers to take on your fantasy waiver wire this week than Vidal. The Chargers could start unloading players soon, and depending on how that goes, he could find himself in an improved situation — there or with another team."

It remains to be seen what Los Angeles decides to do with its team as the team looks to avoid being 0-6 on Sunday against the Chiefs.

articles.title: 3 storylines for Alabama vs. Tennessee in Top 25 road showdown
articles.summary: Alabama travels to Neyland Stadium on Saturday, a venue they have struggled at in recent trips. Here are three storylines entering Saturday's game.
articles.body:
Similar to last week against Georgia, this Saturday afternoon's matchup between Alabama and Tennessee is loaded with potential storylines.

To start, this is the latest chapter in one of the SEC's greatest long-standing rivalries known as "The Third Saturday in October." Alabama and Tennessee have a lengthy history which dates back to the early 1900's, with the Crimson Tide owning a 61-39-8 all-time advantage in the series.

During the Nick Saban era, the rivalry was essentially owned by Alabama, aside from a 2022 victory for Tennessee in Knoxville. Since Kalen DeBoer arrived in Tuscaloosa, Alabama owns a 1-1 record against Tennessee where they fell in Knoxville back in 2024, but avenged that loss a year ago at home.

The latest chapter of the rivalry will once again feature a pair of ranked teams, both of which have impressed up to this point in the season. Both the Crimson Tide and Volunteers sit at 5-1 overall (2-1 SEC).

Let's take a look at three storylines to know entering Saturday's latest matchup between the Crimson Tide and Vols in Knoxville.

Can Alabama reverse recent trends in Neyland?

The Crimson Tide have simply not played well during their last two trips to Knoxville, losing a pair of one-possession games in 2022 and 2024 by final scores of 52-49 and 24-17, respectively. In those close losses, Alabama struggled significantly with penalties committing a combined 32 between the two games, as well as in run defense where the Volunteers had 396 yards on the ground with an average of nearly five yards per carry. The Crimson Tide also had a rough showing in 2024 on third-and-fourth down, going 4-of-16.

Will Alabama defense bounce back against Tennessee run game?

Speaking of Alabama's run defense, this was an area where the Crimson Tide struggled a week ago against Georgia, and will certainly be tested Saturday afternoon in Knoxville. Alabama gave up 206 yards, as well as an average of 5.3 yards per carry, on the ground a week ago to Georgia, and will now face a Tennessee ground game that ranks No. 2 in the SEC with an average of 228.3 yards a contest.

Will Kalen DeBoer continue success coming off a loss?

As the head coach at Alabama, Kalen DeBoer currently owns a 7-1 record coming off a loss, with the lone defeat the 2025 season-opener at Florida State which followed a 2024 bowl game loss to Michigan. When revisiting those wins since 2024, only one of those seven victories was decided in a one-possession game (South Carolina in 2024).

articles.title: Valkyries reach record $100M in annual revenue as world's most valuable women's sports franchise
articles.summary: The Valkyries have become the first professional women's sports team to generate $100 million in annual revenue, adding another milestone to their second sea...
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries have become the first professional women's sports team to generate $100 million in annual revenue, adding another milestone to a season that has drawn sold-out crowds and helped make the franchise the most valuable team in not just the WNBA, but across all of women's sports.

The Valkyries will face the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for 12:30 p.m. Saturday at Chase Center, where fans have packed the arena throughout the season.

Among them is Jennifer Ling of Foster City, a season-ticket holder who said she has spent heavily supporting the team.

"My wallet doesn't love me right now. I came here to get some finals merch," Ling said.

Ling said she has spent more than $1,000 on the team over the past two years.

A supporter since the franchise's launch, Ling said, "I was really stoked to be a part of something special."

Fans say the Valkyries' success extends beyond the court.

"I have an 8-year-old daughter. To see her excitement around this is awesome," fan Dalan McNabola said.

The team's business performance has also drawn attention. This year, the Valkyries became the first professional women's sports team to generate $100 million in annual revenue. According to Sportico , the franchise is valued at $850 million, an astonishing number in just their second year that puts them at the top of all women's sports teams.

"It is super exciting, especially for an expansion team to do this in year two is incredible," McNabola said.

Sports columnist Bruce Jenkins said the Valkyries have become a model for the league and for women's sports more broadly.

"This is what the WNBA has always wanted to be and it is right here. And they are setting the standard," Jenkins said.

Nola Agha, a professor of sport management at the University of San Francisco, said the franchise's success is rooted in strong leadership and execution.

"They have an amazing ownership group and they have an amazing president who know how to monetize and who know how to run a really professional franchise," Agha said.

"They're hiring great coaches, great players, and they know how to win," she added.

Agha also credited the team's devoted fan base.

"This team is tapping into a fan base that's never had the opportunity to purchase tickets to an exciting game, to an exciting product," Agha said. "There's lots of excited fans in women's basketball."

With sold-out crowds at Chase Center, the Valkyries continue to draw enthusiastic support as they prepare for the WNBA FInals.

articles.title: No Excuses: Jim Leonhard Tells Bills Defense 'It's Time To Be Good At Something'
articles.summary: Jim Leonhard’s patience is being tested by a porous Buffalo Bills defense that’s giving up too many points, too many yards and having difficulty stopping opponents on fourth down.
articles.body: Jim Leonhard’s patience is being tested by a porous Buffalo Bills defense that’s giving up too many points, too many yards and having difficulty stopping opponents on fourth down. And the first-year defensive coordinator is done making excuses regarding a new-look unit experiencing growing pains five weeks into the season. "It’s time to be good at something, and that’s our struggles right now," Leonhard said. "It’s too inconsistent to pretend that we’re building and working and making improvements. Everything’s being evaluated." Leonhard maintained confidence in his players, but cautioned the next step could involve roster changes. "This is professional football. If we don’t feel like the answers are there then, yeah, then there gets to be some big conversations," he said. Leonhard addressed reporters over a Zoom conference call on Tuesday, a day after quarterback Josh Allen bailed out the defense in a 37-34 overtime win at the Los Angeles Rams. The Bills (4-1) are staying in Southern California before leaving for Las Vegas to face the Raiders (3-2) on Sunday. In thanking Allen for playing what he called the role of Superman, Leonhard said relying on the offense to carry the load isn’t a recipe for success. "It has to change. It has to get better," he said. "We plan on being in a lot of big games, and it’s our job as a defense to go close them out for wins." Familiar Issues Keep Cropping Up And while the Rams high-octane attack presented a steep degree of difficulty, he said it doesn’t make up for the ongoing problems that continue arising. __ Buffalo allowed 33 first downs against LA, matching the most the defense has surrendered dating to 1991. The Bills have allowed 20 or more first downs in each of their five outings, one short of last season’s total. __ A re-shuffled secondary experienced coverage and communication issues in allowing Matthew Stafford's 383 yards passing. The Bills have allowed 250 or more yards passing four times already, twice more than last year. __ Fourth-down stops are a problem, with Buffalo allowing opponents to convert 8 of 9 attempts after the Rams went 2-for-2. __ The inability to get off the field is not only reflected in Buffalo allowing the third-most yards per outing (389) and fifth-most points (141) in the NFL thus far, it’s tiring out a unit that’s played 350 snaps, the second most behind Detroit. "You play that many snaps, it’s hard to sustain," Leonhard said, referring to the defense playing 78 snaps on Monday — the most by Buffalo since 2023. "We have to get some bigger wins earlier in the game," he added. "I have to be more aggressive in helping us get off the field in some situations to help these guys not get to that fourth quarter and be burned out." In taking over the defense following Sean McDermott's firing, Leonhard anticipated more from a unit entering the season making the switch to a 3-4 system and breaking in four new starters. Though injuries have played a role, the weak spot has involved the secondary, with the starting cornerback position unsettled opposite Christian Benford. After starting the first four games, second-year player Maxwell Hairston was replaced by rookie Davison Igbinosun on Monday. The Bills' depth was already thin at the position in opening the season with five cornerbacks, including Dee Alford filling the nickel position. Part of the problem, Leonard said, is players trying to do too much. "There’s a fine line of trying harder and trying smarter," he said. "I have that tendency. You want to do more, you want to do extra. Sometimes, it’s just relax, take a step back and simplify. Slow down." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Tiger Woods & Girlfriend Vanessa Trump Dealt Unfortunate News
articles.summary: Tiger Woods and his girlfriend Vanessa Trump were dealt bad news on Wednesday. The latter’s daughter, Kai, started as a freshman golfer at the University of...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods and his girlfriend Vanessa Trump were dealt bad news on Wednesday. The latter's daughter, Kai, started as a freshman golfer at the University of Miami this year.

She committed in August 2024 and signed in November 2025. She made her college debut Sept. 6-8 at the Golfweek Fall Challenge in Pawleys Island.

But Kai got herself injured in the event. She hurt her wrist when she struck the ground beside a cart path. The pain worsened when she hit her driver later.

She had surgery on her left wrist back in January. After the September injury, follow-up testing showed no complete tear. Kai received stem cell injections in hopes of avoiding surgery.

Kai kept competing. But on Oct. 14, she shared more about her injury.

Kai said she had hoped to avoid surgery but underwent the operation anyway.

"I recently underwent surgery to repair a wrist injury I sustained during my first tournament of the season," she said . "While I had hoped to avoid surgery, after talks with my family, coaches, and athletic training staff, I know I made the best decision for my long-term health and my future in the game I love. It's certainly not how I envisioned the next few months, but sometimes the journey takes an unexpected turn, and I'm choosing to embrace this one with patience and a whole lot of determination."

Kai said she decided after talks with her family, coaches and athletic training staff. But that decision also must have included Woods. The 15-time major champion is a major role model for her.

Woods is especially close with Kai. He advised the 19-year-old before her LPGA Tour debut at The Annika in November 2025.

Kai praised Woods at the ESPYs in New York on July 15. "He's inspired me a lot," she told Us Weekly . "Just to be a better person, better golfer, and stuff like that."

Woods also attended Kai's graduation May 15, Page Six reported . The ceremony took place at The Benjamin School in Palm Beach Gardens, Fla. He arrived about 15 minutes late and left about 20 minutes early, the outlet said. He skipped the family dinner that followed, according to the outlet.

Woods was in a treatment program in Switzerland in May. He put a pin in his rehab and returned to Florida from Switzerland to attend her graduation. The two are really close.

articles.title: West Indies beat India to level T20 series as Hope continues record run
articles.summary: Shai Hope’s 102 gives West Indies a 24-run series-leveling win over India in fourth cricket T20 as another record falls.
articles.body:
Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2.

Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl.

It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.

In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs.

Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s.

Bengaluru will host the deciding T20 on Saturday.

Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). Axar Patel trapped Andrew lbw in the fifth over but West Indies still got 79-1 in the powerplay.

Hope then added another 58 off 24 balls with Shimron Hetmyer, reaching 50 off 28 balls with the help of five sixes. He sped to a second hundred in the series with another four sixes.

Hope also became only the fifth batter to score multiple hundreds in a bilateral T20 series. Overall, it was his fourth hundred in seven innings across ODIs and T20s on this tour.

He wasn’t finished, despite Prince Yadav sending back Hetmyer for 33, while Rovman Powell scored 24.

Sherfane Rutherford scored 49 not out off 26 balls to provide the final flourish, hitting four fours and three sixes, as West Indies breached 200.

Hope and Rutherford added 91 off only 43 balls, as India served a slow over-rate penalty in the final over. Nitish Reddy gave away 19 runs in the 20th, with Hope reaching his century with a six off the last ball.

In reply, Samson hit four sixes to give India a quick start. He and Abhishek Sharma (29) added 60 off 25 balls as India scored 80-2 in the powerplay.

Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over – Samson was out caught at square leg on the first ball and then three balls later, Ishan Kishan was caught at deep mid wicket for six.

India also lost skipper Shreyas Iyer (16) before the halfway mark, and was down to 97-3.

Abhishek Sharma didn’t get going, scoring 29 off 24 balls, with three fours and a six. His dismissal was the turning point – he was caught off Gudakesh Motie at long off in the 12th over.

Motie also had Naman Dhir stumped for a golden duck.

Tilak Varma fought hard with 43 off 25 balls along with Nitish Reddy’s cameo (41 off 20 balls) but it went in vain.

Paul picked three wickets in the 19th over to wrap up the innings.

articles.title: Rutgers Football vs Maryland 2026 Preview
articles.summary: Battle at the bottom of the Big Ten
articles.body:
After having a bye week last Saturday, Rutgers football will return to action this weekend as it is set to make the trip down to College Park to play Maryland. The Terrapins, on the other hand, will be coming into this game after suffering a 45-16 loss at the hands of No.5 Ohio State in Columbus. This game will also serve as the homecoming game for Maryland.

Neither squad had a good game their last time out, as both were matched up against the two best teams in the conference, with Rutgers losing 47-15 to then No.6 Indiana. Last game, Maryland quarterback Malik Washington went 12 for 25 passes for 64 yards, while adding five rushes for 19 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan completed five out of 10 passes for 67 yards before being taken out of the game due to injury. (Schiano confirmed he will be the starter for this game)

Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond struggled to get anything going against Indiana as well, recording 11 rushes for just 31 yards. The same was true for DeJuan Williams, who recorded 16 rushes for 48 yards. Maryland's top receiver against Ohio State was Chris Durr Jr., who recorded four catches for 15 yards. Durr Jr. has 476 yards on 46 catches as well as four touchdowns for the season. KJ Duff once again led Rutgers in receiving, recording four catches for 78 yards. Duff has 628 yards and seven touchdowns on 33 catches this season.

Both defenses had rough outings last week, with both surrendering at least 400 yards and 40 points to their opponent.

Rutgers opened as 4.5-point underdogs against Maryland, in a game where many fans believe it's the Knights' best chance to win a Big Ten game all season. (Aside from maybe Michigan State) One way or another, one team is going to be walking out of this game with their first Big Ten win of the season. Despite it likely being to little, to late, it will be interesting to see what adjustments Rutgers has made in the bye week, especially on the defensive side of the ball. That extra week to plan could prove vital in this matchup.

articles.title: Seahawks injury update: Drake Thomas ruled out vs. Broncos

The curse of the short week has hit the Seattle Seahawks ahead of their Thursday night showdown with the Denver Broncos, as the team will be without one of their starting linebackers.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald ruled out linebacker Drake Thomas, running back Zach Charbonnet and linebacker Chazz Surratt on Wednesday. Thomas, who emerged as Ernest Jones IV's partner in crime in 2025, is recovering from an ankle injury he suffered late in the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers last week.

In place of the injured Thomas, Macdonald said the team will lean on the team's 2024 fourth-round pick Tyrice Knight. The UTEP product has had several stints in the starting lineup throughout his three years with the Seahawks, but hasn't found the field much and only recorded one tackle in 2026.

Charbonnet continues his ACL rehab and will not make it back for the pivotal game against the Broncos. The Seahawks running back was so dearly missed last week, but fans will hope for a bounce-back week from Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani, who struggled against the 49ers. Velus Jones Jr. appears to be the other running back option after the Seahawks added him to their active roster on Wednesday .

There may be positive news on Charbonnet soon, at least according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, who reported that there is a "legitimate chance" that the Seahawks back returns in Week 7.

Surratt mostly serves as a special teams player, so it wouldn't be shocking to see the team elevate wide reciever Irv Charles from the practice squad to bolster that unit and give them more positional flexibility.

A mostly healthy Seahawks team will head to Denver and look to get back on track this Thursday at 5:15 p.m.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin Shares Sign a Team’s Season is ‘Dead’
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin reveals when he knew a team's season was over.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin reveals when he knew a team's season was over.

The Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 season has already been full of ups and downs just five weeks in, and their season could still go either way. However, former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin recently shared how he knew a team's season was over.

"What do you think when your team is having a players-only meeting," Jason Kelce asked on his New Heights podcast .

"I think you're dead," Tomlin stated. "If it did occur, I'd like to not hear about it. The fact that you hear about it is what makes it B.S."

Coach Tomlin knows, if your team is having a players-only meeting your season is COOKED NEW EPISODE OUT NOW !!!! @allstate pic.twitter.com/s7BxDm4Hsg — New Heights (@newheightshow) October 14, 2026

Coach Tomlin knows, if your team is having a players-only meeting your season is COOKED NEW EPISODE OUT NOW !!!! @allstate pic.twitter.com/s7BxDm4Hsg

New Heights (@newheightshow) October 14, 2026

Now, Tomlin wasn't specifically talking about the Steelers . In fact, he was talking about the Dallas Cowboys, whose defense reportedly had a players-only meeting following their latest Week 5 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

However, the Steelers are still connected in a way, given their recent trade relationship with the Cowboys, sending offensive tackle Broderick Jones , wide receiver George Pickens , and most recently, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas.

The Cowboys now sit in third place in the NFC East with a 2-3 record, adding to the old sentiment that the grass isn't always greener on the other side.

Tomlin didn't delve any deeper into the matter of players-only meetings and if any of the teams he has coached over the years had one.

But he certainly makes a strong point about the state of the team if it feels as though it needs to resort to a meeting without the coaches.

articles.title: College Football TV Ratings: Tracking the most-watched games of the 2026 season
articles.summary: Last year, college football saw its TV ratings surge and looked to keep the trend going in 2026. On3 is tracking the most-watched games of the season, accord...
articles.body:
Last year, college football saw its TV ratings surge and looked to keep the trend going in 2026. On3 is tracking the most-watched games of the season, according to Nielsen Big Data + Panel data compiled weekly.

Through the first four weeks, Texas' thrilling comeback win over Ohio State emerged as the top game of the college football season. It was the first game of the year to hit 10 million viewers, averaging nearly 14 million as part of the Week 2 slate.

Here is a look at the Top 10 most-watched games of the 2026 season as of Week 4, which will be updated weekly. Additionally, a TV ratings tracker is below the Top 10 with viewership for every Nielsen-rated college football game of the year.

Note: SEC Network, ACC Network and CBS Sports Network do not pay for Nielsen to measure viewership.

Date/Time: Sept. 12, 7:30 p.m. ET (Week 2) Channel: ABC Viewers: 13.99 million

The biggest game of Week 2 delivered for ABC. Texas' thrilling comeback win over Ohio State became the most-watched game on the schedule with 14.0 million viewers, which was down from last year's game, which brought 16.6 million on FOX.

The Longhorns rallied from a 23-3 deficit entering the fourth quarter to get the 24-23 win over the then-top ranked Buckeyes. Arch Manning threw for a touchdown in that final frame while Hollywood Smothers ran in two scores, including the eventual game-winner.

Date/Time: Oct. 10, 7:30 p.m. ET (Week 6) Channel: ABC Viewers: 12.24 million

ABC's primetime game in Week 6 delivered in a big way. Georgia and Alabama went down to the wire at Bryant-Denny Stadium before the Bulldogs came away with the 20-17 victory in the most-watched game of the week – and the second most-watched of the season, per data compiled by On3 .

Gunner Stockton went 18-for-22 for 249 yards and a touchdown, to one interception, while also adding a rushing touchdown to lead the charge. Georgia also jumped up to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 as a result of the win, coupled with Texas' loss to Oklahoma .

Date/Time: Sept. 19, 7:30 p.m. ET (Week 3) Channel: ABC Viewers: 10.90 million

The top draw in Week 3 delivered as the most-watched game on the schedule. Ole Miss' victory over LSU averaged 10.9 million viewers on ABC to rank as the second-most watched game of the year, according to data compiled by On3.

The game was one of the most anticipated matchups of the year as Lane Kiffin made his return to Oxford for the first time since leaving Ole Miss last season. Trinidad Chambliss stole the show as he completed 33 of 48 passes for 363 yards and two touchdowns in the air, and he ran in what proved to be the game-winning touchdown with 6:14 to go in the fourth quarter.

Date/Time: Oct. 7, 3:30 p.m. ET (Week 6) Channel: ABC Viewers: 9.82 million

The Red River Rivalry provided great theatre in Week 6 as Oklahoma rallied to take down Texas . Tate Sandell sent the game-winning field goal through the uprights as time expired, sealing the Sooners' victory over the Longhorns.

It marked Texas' first loss of the season after a 4-0 start to the year. Oklahoma, meanwhile, got above .500 after two losses prior to the bye week while the defense contained Arch Manning and the Longhorns offense.

Date/Time: Sept. 26, 12 p.m. ET (Week 4) Channel: ABC Viewers: 9.7 million

Defense was the name of the game in Texas' victory over Tennessee at Neyland Stadium. The matchup led off the Week 4 slate and brought a TV ratings win for ABC in its early college football slot as the most-watched game of the week.

Considered the top game of the noon window, Texas' victory brought in 9.7 million viewers for ABC to lead the Week 4 slate. Colin Simmons set a Longhorns program record with 5.5 sacks as Texas held off a late Vols push to get the road win.

Date/Time: Sept. 26, 3:30 p.m. ET (Week 4) Channel: ABC Viewers: 8.3 million

Florida made quite a statement with its Week 4 victory over Ole Miss in Gainesville. The Rebels couldn't stop Jadan Baugh and the Gators' high-powered rushing attack as the game became one of the most-watched of the week with 8.3 million viewers.

Florida skyrocketed up the rankings after the game amid a strong start to the Jon Sumrall era. UF is now 4-0 heading into this week's road matchup against Missouri , which will air in the same 3:30 p.m. ET window on ABC.

Date/Time: Sept. 12, 12 p.m. ET (Week 2) Channel: FOX Viewers: 8.22 million

FOX's Big Noon Saturday game saw one of the upsets in Week 2. Oklahoma's offense struggled mightily against Michigan , and the Wolverines were able to capitalize and get the victory in the early window in front of more than 8 million viewers.

Michigan forced two Oklahoma turnovers, including a fourth-quarter interception of John Mateer that helped set up the go-ahead touchdown. The Sooners had one last chance in the final minute, but the drive stalled out as the Wolverines held on for the 17-10 upset win.

8. Wisconsin vs. Notre Dame (at Lambeau Field)

Date/Time: Sept. 6, 7:30 p.m. ET (Week 1) Channel: NBC Viewers: 7.42 million (8.1 million including Adobe Analytics/Peacock)

One of two Sunday night primetime games in Week 1, Wisconsin kept things close against Notre Dame through two quarters at Lambeau Field. The Fighting Irish pulled away after halftime, though, and got the 41-13 victory to start the season – and NBC scored the most-watched game of the weekend.

The game went directly against Ole Miss vs. Louisville , which took place in Nashville on ABC. Despite that, NBC won the weekend and also got 683,000 viewers via streaming, the network announced Thursday.

Date/Time: Sept. 12, 3:30 p.m. ET (Week 2) Channel: ABC Viewers: 7.28 million

Early on, Kentucky looked like it had an upset on its mind against Alabama after the two teams traded pick-sixes. The Crimson Tide was able to right the ship after halftime, though, and come away with the 45-17 victory in Lexington.

Keelon Russell went 16-of-23 passing for 188 yards and a touchdown, along with three turnovers. Daniel Hill led the rushing attack in the effort with a game-high 104 yards and a touchdown.

Date/Time: Sept. 12, 5:15 p.m. ET (Week 3 – delayed due to weather) Channel: ABC Viewers: 7.01 million

Weather delays had a major impact on Florida State's rematch against Alabama on Saturday. ABC was only able to air the first half as a result, but the partial game still brought in 7.01 million viewers before moving to ESPN2.

Keelon Russell had a monster game as he completed 23 of 30 passes for 320 yards and three touchdowns. He also added a rushing touchdown as Alabama got its revenge against Florida State following last year's upset.

College Football TV Ratings: Full 2026 viewership

In 2025, college football saw TV ratings increase 4% during the regular season and a 9% uptick in minutes consumed, counting the postseason. The College Football Playoff also saw ratings surge in the first year of Nielsen's Big Data + Panel reporting method, as well. This season provides a chance for more of an apples-to-apples comparison.

articles.title: CIAC, Hartford Athletic agree to bring soccer championship games back to Trinity Health Stadium
articles.summary: CIAC, Hartford Athletic agree to another one-year deal for soccer finals at Trinity Health Stadium.
articles.body:
The CIAC and Hartford Athletic have agreed to a one-year deal to again host the CIAC boys and girls soccer championships at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford next month.

CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini said the two organizations agreed to the extension late last week. This is the second straight year that a one-year deal was finalized in October . It is also the second straight year Hartford Athletic has had a new staff, Lungarini said.

"Any time that we have new staff in any venue, it is generally in the best interest of the venue as well as CIAC to engage in a one-year extension," Lungarini said. "It's appropriate that the staff at the venue and the leadership of the venue know and understand what is needed to run a CIAC championship, and it gives the CIAC an opportunity to evaluate that venue under new leadership."

The soccer championship games will be held Nov. 21-22, with four games each day.

All of the soccer finals have been held at Trinity Health since 2021, and the CIAC and Hartford Athletic agreed to a three-year extension in November 2022.

Lungarini said Veterans Stadium in New Britain was also a consideration to host the finals. Veterans has hosted many other CIAC championships in the past, including football. He also said meetings with Hartford Athletic were "exceptional," and he noted the addition of a women's team this past season.

"I'm grateful for our current opportunity to continue to play there and optimistic to work with Hartford Athletic in order to provide our kids with a great soccer experience," Lungarini said.

articles.title: Illinois QB Katin Houser sidelined with injury ahead of Oregon matchup
articles.summary: A week before Oregon heads to Illinois, the Illini announced they will be without their starting quarterback for several weeks.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks aren't the only team in the Big Ten turning to a backup quarterback in October. The Ducks will even benefit from facing a backup next week when they hit the road and travel to the Midwest.

Illinois quarterback Katin Houser started the first six games of the season for the Illini, but now he is set to miss significant time. Head coach Bret Bielema announced on Wednesday that Houser suffered a broken left hand in the team's overtime win last week against Michigan State. Although it is Houser's non-throwing hand, the senior quarterback is expected to miss four to six weeks after surgery.

In his stead, freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II became the problem fixer and led the Illini to a win over the Spartans . He will likely command the role again when the Ducks make their trip to Champaign next weekend. The Illini have a bye week this week, so Clayton will get extra time to work with the starters in practice before facing Oregon's defense.

Houser was a solid starter this season for Illinois, completing 66.3% of his passes and throwing for 1,440 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. He also ran for 120 yards. Clayton entered last week's game and completed 6-of-8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. He threw the game-winning touchdown on the first play of overtime.

Illinois seems to have plenty of confidence in the freshman to lead the offense. Bielema previously named sophomore Carson Boyd as the backup, but when forced to make a decision, he turned to Clayton instead. Clayton is a former three-star recruit with multiple Power 4 offers. Standing at 6-foot-4, Clayton is a pocket passer who doesn't run much, but he is difficult to bring down.

The Illini need to win three more games to make a bowl game, and Clayton can use this runway to prove himself as the potential starter next season, so there is a lot on the line. After putting together a solid showing off the bench against Michigan State, Oregon has a little bit of tape on Clayton, who is set to make his first collegiate start against the Ducks on Oct. 24.

The Ducks still need to figure out their own quarterback situation as well. If Dante Moore doesn't return this week against Nebraska or next week against Illinois, Oregon will need to find a long-term solution with either Dylan Raiola or Brock Thomas.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB misses Wednesday practice
articles.summary: Rookie RB Jeremiyah Love's ankle is still bothering him.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals began their week of practice on Wednesday to get ready for the Los Angeles Rams , and there was one notable absence — rookie running back Jeremiyah Love. Head coach Mike LaFleur, prior to practice, said Love would be held out of practice, as the rookie continues to deal with a lingering ankle injury, the second he has suffered this year.

He wouldn't say whether Love would miss the game on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams, opting to say they will take things "one day at a time," noting he and the team "want to get this ankle right and do it the right way."

Love came back from a high ankle sprain from the preseason in a way that LaFleur called "unbelievable," saying that the first injury doesn't bother Love at all. It is the other ankle that has been lingering.

He was not on the field in the open part of practice, and when the first injury report of the week is released, he will be listed as a non-participant.

There has been some discussion about shutting Love down for a bit, perhaps putting him on injured reserve to heal, but that would mean he can't even practice. "We're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give it a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday," he said.

The ankle injury limited Love for two days in practice last week before he was a full participant and then had not game designation on the Cardinals' final Week 5 injury report. We will see how things progress this week.

Love rushed for 22 yards on 12 carries on Sunday and has 245 rushing yards and a touchdown on the season, averaging 3.7 yards per attempt.

articles.title: 5-Star Wing AJ Williams Set to Visit BYU; What are BYU’s Chances?
articles.summary: BYU is getting its top 2027 target on campus as 5-star wing AJ Williams will begin his official visit October 15. Brandon Jenkins of 247 Sports was the first...
articles.body:
BYU is getting its top 2027 target on campus as 5-star wing AJ Williams will begin his official visit October 15. Brandon Jenkins of 247 Sports was the first to report the visit.

Williams will attend the BYU-Nebraska exhibition game Friday night and should be able to take part in the College Gameday festivities on Saturday. Sources tell me that BYU has been targeting this weekend for some time so Williams could attend the Nebraska exhibition and BYU-Notre Dame game.

As I detailed back in September , AJ Williams has been BYU's top target in the 2027 class. Kevin Young has made it clear that he will target a 5-Star guard/wing in each class, and BYU is trying to make AJ Williams follow in the footsteps of Egor Demin, AJ Dybantsa, and Bruce Branch. The recruiting pitch for Williams is simple — Kevin Young can turn on the tape for each of those guys and show how he will use AJ and what he can do to prepare him for the NBA.

The Georgia native has already taken official visits to Auburn, Mississippi State, and Georgia. Industry sources have told me that BYU is considered the front runner at the moment. This official visit could get BYU closer to sealing the deal. The opportunity to play in Kevin Young's system and be featured in BYU's offense is intriguing to AJ, sources have told me. This isn't a done deal yet, however, and home state school Georgia particularly is a threat.

AJ Williams was the #1 recruit in the 2028 class until he reclassified to 2027, where 247 Sports rates him at #5. Listed at 6-foot-7, AJ is a dynamic scorer and shot creator who can fit into the mold of what BYU did with AJ Dybantsa. While he isn't the prospect Dybantsa was (I mean, nobody really is) he is a wing scorer who BYU would feature and build around.

AJ was part of Chris Paul's AAU team, who has a very close relationship with Kevin Young and has told AJ what KY can do for him. AJ Dybantsa and Rob Wright attended one of Williams' AAU events in the spring and saw him play and spoke to him then.

There have been conversations about Bronny James' effectiveness on the LA Lakers, and coach JJ Redick discussed his progress on Tuesday. Some fans thought his remarks contained a subtle shot.

James, drafted in the second round in 2024, has received modest playing time in his first two seasons, averaging 2.7 points per game in 69 games. He has gotten consistent minutes in the preseason but has failed to produce anything noteworthy. In the Lakers' 101-89 loss to the Golden State Warriors on Tuesday, he played 11 minutes without scoring. He is averaging 2.8 ppg, shooting 26.7%, in 17.8 minutes per game in the preseason.

While addressing his four-game stretch after the game, Redick said:

"I don't think he's played well in the four preseason games, but he's had good practices. … Some of it is, like, the group he's with; I think that is not necessarily setting him up for success."

However, one fan suggested Redick indirectly took a dig at James:

Austin Reaves was stellar, scoring 28 points on 10-for-18 shooting while adding four rebounds and seven assists in 25 minutes. Walker Kessler also joined the squad for the first time, scoring 11 points and grabbing nine rebounds in 16 minutes.

The Lakers center believes the team shared the ball well

Walker Kessler looked good in his preseason debut for the Lakers on Tuesday. He is expected to make a big impact in the Lakers' frontcourt, which has drastically underperformed in the last few seasons. Although the Lakers lost, Kessler believed the team looked good:

"It was a lot of fun being out there again. You know, it's been so long. … We shared the ball really well tonight."

The Lakers had a chance at the title last season. With LeBron James out of the picture, Kessler has some big shoes to fill while the team looks for another title-contending season.

The Bengals return from their bye week to face AFC North rival the Baltimore Ravens in Maryland on Sunday, Oct. 25.

The matchup comes after Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson sustained an ankle injury during the second half of Baltimore's Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans . He was ruled out for the team's "Sunday Night Football" matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Oct. 11.

As for his return, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson's status for Week 6 against the Cleveland Browns is unknown. So Bengals fans will have to wait and see if Jackson gears up in Week 7.

"To Lamar's credit, this dude's working his tail off to get back," Minter said. "He's in there all the time. Don't know the specifics of next week, but he'll be doing everything in his power to get back."

Former Bengal-turned-Raven Trey Hendrickson was also ruled out for Sunday night's game. He has not practiced since undergoing surgery for his finger injury during Week 4. It seems unlikely the linebacker will return for the Bengals.

articles.title: Dan Miller’s Message For Lions Fans After Personal Tragedy
articles.summary: Late last week, Detroit Lions radio commentator Dan Miller experienced an unimaginable tragedy when his wife Cynthia succumbed to cancer at only 63 years of...
articles.body:
Late last week, Detroit Lions radio commentator Dan Miller experienced an unimaginable tragedy when his wife Cynthia succumbed to cancer at only 63 years of age.

Understandably, Miller was not in the broadcast booth at State Farm Stadium during Detroit's 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals; the game ball was awarded to Miller from afar by head coach Dan Campbell.

Miller has since come forward with a message of thanks for Lions fans everywhere who had been sending him and their family well wishes following the loss of Cynthia.

Detroit Lions Commentator Dan Miller Sends Message Of Thanks To Fans

Miller called into FOX 2's "The Sports Office" and had a message of gratitude for Lions fans who had been sending him and the rest of the family their well wishes following the loss of Cynthia.

"I can't express enough how much it has meant to me and my family, and how healing it has been to me and my family as we work our way through this," Miller said.

Miller also explained that Cynthia had been experiencing a rare and, sadly, incurable form of cancer.

"It's a terminal disease, it's incurable, and you're basically just trying to buy time," Miller said. "We did buy some time. We were blessed to buy some time. But we knew we were going to lose her at some point, and we did. It's a very rare form of cancer. It's not one that a lot of people are familiar with, and it's not one that a lot of people get. But it is one that we need to find some way to attack and find some better treatments for so that when people get it, they have a chance to extend life as long as possible."

Dan Miller Is Truly Appreciative Of The Outpouring Of Love His Family Is Receiving

While Miller and his family are going through an unimaginable time right now, they can take some comfort in the fact that they're being embraced by Lions fans as a whole, and being kept in their thoughts and prayers.

"To see people respond like that has meant the world to us. And, honestly, not just the donations, but everybody that has reached out, everybody that has sent condolences, everybody that has sent—just saying they're thinking about us, it means the world," Miller said. "I've honestly tried to sit down and craft something on social media and I could never find the words. I could never find the appropriate tone. I could never find enough to cover my wife, our loss, her battle, the kindness of people, and just how it all meets at some point to the point where we're at in our lives, and just how important they've been helping us get through these couple of days.

"Look, I'm well acquainted with One Pride and Lions fans, and I'm well acquainted with sports fans in Detroit. But when you're in the vortex of something that we've been in here, and you feel their kindness and it's right there aimed at you and your family, words can't express how much it means."

articles.title: Dodgers fans head for the exits as NLCS nightmare reaches new low
articles.summary: Dodgers fans exit early in an NLCS Game 3 matchup.It’s been one of those nights for the Los Angeles Dodgers, and their fans are headed straight for the exit...
articles.body:
It's been one of those nights for the Los Angeles Dodgers, and their fans are headed straight for the exit gates.

Before the Dodgers suffered a 6-2 loss in the NLCS on Wednesday night , fans were already leaving the stadium before the ninth inning.

California Post senior sports reporter Edward Lewis captured multiple videos of fans exiting the stadium behind the bleachers in centerfield.

The news of the Dodgers leaving early came after they failed to fill out the stadium.

From the game's opening pitch until the final out, Dodger Stadium was littered with empty seats , with the colors of blue and yellow chairs sprinkled throughout — even though the cost of tickets plummeted by 42% before the game began.

With Wednesday's loss, the Dodgers are now facing a 3-0 deficit in the series and are a game away from being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers.

The Dodgers spent most of the game trailing the Brewers after Jackson Chourio made history on the game's opening pitch.

Chourio saw a fastball come his way on the first pitch of the game and sent it over the right center-field fence for a solo home run.

Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell settled in from there, striking out nine batters through six innings.

Los Angeles got their first lead of the game in the sixth, when Will Smith, who spent most of his day welcoming his newborn child had a chance to make a difference for his team .

With the bases loaded and only one out, Smith hit a two-RBI double to score Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernandez.

Through most of the postseason, the Dodgers have struggled to bring runners home while in scoring position, and did just that after Smith's rally starter as he and Shohei Ohtani were left stranded on third and second after Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman were struck out to end the inning.

Snell entered the seventh and gave up only two hits and one walk. The Brewers doubled that production and made it count .

Jake Bauers worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Snell in the inning and finished it with a two-run homer to end the game. Garrett Mitchell followed in the next at-bat by launching a changeup that was left hanging over the middle of the plate, 428 feet towards center field to make it a 4-2 game.

Milwaukee tacked on one more run in the eighth, sending the fans home. After they left, Joey Ortiz hit an RBI single to left to give the game its final score.

As the Dodgers are on the verge of being swept in the playoffs for the first time since 2023, they will host Milwaukee for Game 4 on Thursday at 6:00 p.m. PT.
